stories.title: Yaxel Lendeborg poured fuel on fire, awakened the beast in Luka Doncic
stories.summary: The Warriors rookie did not regret his comments, but he will.
stories.detailText: Yaxel Lendeborg, there are a few things you have to learn. Never take a charge from LeBron James. Never challenge Victor Wembanyama at the rim. And never trash-talk Luka Dončić. The last sin is the worst. The consequences are worse than a bruise. Or a swatted shot. Dončić punishes his perpetrators over and over again, leaving them mortified and stammering after games. Or at least, that’s how this usually goes. Lendeborg committed the last sin in the Lakers’ 127-105 win over the Warriors in their season opener on Wednesday. The Warriors’ rookie ran his mouth. The Slovenian superstar ran him over. No biggie. We’ve seen this play out so many times before. But what happened next was rare. The rookie didn’t show remorse. Instead he doubled down. Here’s how it all happened. Things heated up after the rookie fouled Dončić on a pump fake with the Lakers up, 53-48, and less than 3 minutes left in the second quarter. Dončić made two free throws. Lendeborg went to the bench. Doncic then made a 15-foot jumper and pointed at Lendeborg. Warriors coach Steve Kerr put him back in the game. They continued trash-talking each other. Lendeborg was assessed a technical foul with 22.2 seconds left. Dončić then made a 49-foot shot with 1.4 seconds remaining and approached Lendeborg, chirping at him. Yaxel Lendeborg on Luka: "I had a lot of respect for him. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect." "I was telling him he sucks. He can't score on me" pic.twitter.com/EGwxqR8k8f https://t.co/LkaKZ1Qc7A — Ballislife.com (@Ballislife) October 22, 2026 Yaxel Lendeborg (1) of the Golden State Warriors plays defense on Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers during a game at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Dončić did what he does. He feeds off of perceived disrespect. It fueled a 13-4 run for the Lakers in which Doncic scored 10 points. He finished with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and three steals in 30 minutes and the highest plus-minus (+31) of anyone on the court in the Lakers’ 22-point rout. He had more than twice as many points as Lendeborg (12). Lendeborg poked the bear, like many have before. (Just ask Matas Buzelis, who unleashed a 51-point performance from Doncic last March after chirping at him. His lesson? “Probably not to talk to him,” Buzelis said after the Bulls’ 142-130 loss to the Lakers .) But that’s where the script changes. Lendeborg didn’t drop the bear-poking stick. Instead he picked it up and started beating the mammal over the head with it. “I had a lot of respect for him…seeing him kill people all the time,” Lendeborg said. “But then being in there firsthand and just watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect, man. That was awful. “Me getting frustrated it’s not about the foul being called. It’s about him complaining the entire game. And then you get the foul call, congratulations bro. And then you talk to me like you did something great, bro? Come on, dog. That’s just weak. It kind of threw me off for a little while because, like I said, I had so much respect for him. Gone, man. Gone.” Golden State Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg looks on during an NBA basketball game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Cue the eerie music. The Lakers play the Warriors again in a little over a week on October 30. This could get ugly for Lendeborg. Don’t be surprised if Doncic, who led the league in scoring last season with 33.5 points per game, erupts for twice that number. Lendeborg just fed Dončić his version of basketball mana. He just gave him a performance-enhancing drug. He poured fuel over the fire. “I think everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you get a different me,” Doncic said in his walk-off interview with ESPN. And that was before Lendeborg sounded off in his postgame interview. Golden State Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg (1) plays defense during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images He had more to say, too. “I was telling him he sucks,” Lendeborg continued when asked what he told Doncic. “He can’t score on me. You talk and you can’t score on me. I said it the whole game. I said a couple of cuss words, obviously, that’s why I got the technical and all that. But I was letting him know because he was laughing and talking and all this because of that one call. His only bucket on me was a banker from half court. “I know it’s a team sport. What did he have? He had 28 on us as a team. Me, I took my matchup personally. Tried not to get called on the fouls. Tried my best. I was thinking about playing him with my hands behind my back to see if that worked. Probably still would’ve gotten a foul called.” You can almost imagine Dončić sitting at home and listening to this while rubbing his hands together. Lendeborg’s teammates had his back, defending the team’s No. 11 draft pick whom Draymond Green recently called “the next face of the franchise” on his podcast, “The Draymond Green Show.” Said Green: “Everybody’s going to be like, oh man, he shouldn’t talk to Luka, you shouldn’t talk to Luka. And I disagree with that s—t 1,000%. If you’re going to go talk to somebody, you talk until you can’t f—king talk no more. And if he busts your ass, guess what? You play him again three more times and you go back at his ass again.” Added Steph Curry: “He set the table for himself to have to show up — and I like that.” Well, this is going to be fun. In his first game of his NBA career, Lendeborg put a target on his back. And he did it against one of the top-four players in the league. The 24-year-old has moxie. He’s not lacking in confidence. He’s not afraid of anyone. But come October 30, he should be.

stories.title: How much of a weapon is the Lakers’ new depth?
stories.summary: The Lakers have depth this season, which should allow them to be even more of a threat this season.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 21: Al Horford #20 of the Golden State Warriors battles Sandro Mamukelashvili #54 of the Los Angeles Lakers for position during the second half of a game at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The start of the regular season brought with it lots to be happy about in Tuesday’s rout of the Warriors. The new Big 3 had huge nights and gave the Lakers a great opening to the season. Prior to all that, we asked for questions and you guys delivered, as always. Obviously, some of this will come with a caveat of it coming before that opening game, but all of it still applies. So, let’s dive into what you want to talk about. JJ claims he has a roster that fits together now and is deep….does that mean he will refrain from playing Luka and Austin 45 minutes a game? — Reality Check 1617 I continue to say this sentiment is overblown, but I also acknowledge, and I think JJ would, too, that he couldn’t rely on his bench as much this year. By all accounts, that should change. Again, he even said as much in his media availability at the start of the season. We’ll have to see if the action meet the words, but, on paper, this is a deeper team that should mean everyone plays fewer minutes, particularly the stars. The fact they went nine deep on Tuesday with Collin Sexton and Adou Thiero injured further drives home that belief, though. When at full health — which will likely happen rarely this season — this team could go 10 or 11 deep. That should allow them lots of rest for lots of guys, stars included. How much should we be worried about our scouting, player development, and drafting departments? I know we’ve been hiring and changing since the ownership changes, but how much can we count on this fresh start and new personnel being a new direction? — Johnny Tuttle I don’t think worried is the word I would use, but excited. It’s no secret the Lakers have been well behind the curve when it comes to scouting. That fact is laid bare in the team whiffing on Jalen Hood-Schifino and Dalton Knecht back-to-back years. Beefing up those areas should address a clear weakness in the franchise. Think about how many positions the Lakers have filled this year that just didn’t exist prior. There are not just more knowledgeable voices in the mix, but ones with decades of experience, too. For so long, the Lakers kept such a small inner circle in the front office. Seeing that expand to include more smart voices is a very, very welcome change. What is the back story on the trade of Ayton? On the surface, it made and makes little sense to have traded a guy who, yeah, was ‘meh’ as a starter but would have been well above average as a back-up. Lakers got back relatively little and since then have been searching for a backup center…when they had just traded a good one. So: -is it that they had another trade lined up for a back up center but it fell through? -is it that Ayton was a locker room cancer who they just wanted to be rid of whatever his skills? -is it that they think Looney is a better fit? -is it…just a miscalculation? — scooter I think this is one of those situations where things are better on better than they are in practice. On paper, the Lakers had an underwhelming starting center who was still talented on an affordable contract. After acquiring their starting center, Ayton made sense as the backup where so much wasn’t riding on his shoulders. In practice, and with a bit of reading between the lines, Ayton was…a lot. While we laughed at the idea of the training staff giving him Crunk Juice to motivate him , the amount of massaging of his personality, so to speak, only for him not to really show up when needed was probably grating. He was proclaiming that he wasn’t Clint Capela when that’s exactly what the Lakers needed. The team was wearing shirts with half of his face and half of a lion . All that for him to be unplayable against the Thunder was a lot. Sure, in a backup role, responsibilities and expectations change. But I just think the Lakers were ready to be out of the Ayton business. And the fact that they could get draft capital back for him was all the more reason to be done. I think their calculation was that going into the season looking for a backup center with some extra draft capital was better than another season of the Ayton experience. As I understand, the first that the Lakers can trade Bronny is December 15th. Am I correct on that? As such, shouldn’t they stick him in the G League where he can actually rack up stat lines and possibly increase his trade value? — OCLakerFan1968 The Lakers play the Sixers twice this season. The first game is on December 25th in LA. What are the chances that the Lakers’ marketing department capitalizes on the historic nature of Father versus Son and have Bronny start? — Crap After a very poor preseason, it’s fair to be low on Bronny. Even if he was dealing with an injury that predated training camp, that feels like the kind of story you put out to save face after the fact. I’ve had some questions about how the Lakers are developing Bronny, or what they’re developing him into. He’s always felt like more of an Avery Bradley type as a small off-ball guard with a focus on defense and shooting. But a lot of his reps have come as an on-ball point guard type, which doesn’t make as much sense. Regardless of what his role should be, it’s pretty clear now that the scouting report says to pressure Bronny and he can’t deal with it. And until that changes, he’s probably not going to get any consistent minutes. Having said that, there’s zero value in putting him back in the G League. He’s already shown he’s a great G League player. No team is going to trade for him because he had a couple of good G League games. It’s sink-or-swim time for Bronny in the big leagues. At some point, you have to find out what you have and the Lakers are going to do that this season. If it doesn’t work, then they decline his option for next year and cut bait. As for the latter point, I know it was at least partly written in jest, but I don’t imagine head coach JJ Redick has much interest in sentimental stuff with LeBron James anymore. What is our biggest positional with this current roster? Backup PG – We saw how thin we are if any of Luka/AR/Sexton are resting injuries Backup PF – I guess we are calling Williams and Mamu our PFs? Backup C – Does ANYONE have faith in both Kessler’s health and Looney actually being productive? — Kilgary I think the answer is pretty clearly the backup center spot, and I think the Lakers know that. That’s been the most persistent rumor since this summer. Trades tend not to happen until that Dec. 15 date when most of the league becomes trade-eligible, so I don’t imagine this is something the team will be able to fix for some time. The backup PG position isn’t as bad when Collin Sexton returns. You have four capable ballhandlers. And for the backup power forward, the dearth of wings on the roster are going to man that spot and I don’t think this team will have a “traditional” four. The NBA announced in the off season that the officials would crack down (point of emphasis) on the off-arm push-offs frequently used by players like Harden, and SGA. Was any data released from the pre-season games on whether the officials were calling this violation more frequently than before (knowing that the calls might be fewer if players were policing themselves)? — Coops Knee Highs There hasn’t been and I don’t expect there will be. In the past, the league has never really done something like this when it comes to its points of emphasis. Things could change this year, but that would be a new development. stories.title: The 76ers immediately looked like a contender, and they still have another level to reach
stories.summary: This is what Sixers fans dreamed of, and it can still get so much better.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The inaugural possession of the Philadelphia 76ers’ season opener against the New York Knicks, a 106-100 Sixers win to spoil some of New York’s banner-raising delight, helped convey just how different life may be for each of Philadelphia’s four All-Stars this year, particularly its point guard, Tyrese Maxey. After shuffling up the floor, Maxey delivered the ball to his backcourt mate, VJ Edgecombe, and veered into a bludgeoning back-screen as LeBron James took the baton and initiated the action himself. With the entirety of Philadelphia’s star-laden starting five in transit, New York could not properly traverse the commotion. Worried about James motoring downhill, OG Anunoby was tardy switching onto Maxey, who rainbowed home the catch-and-shoot triple for three of his game-high 28 points. View Link Tuesday night, Maxey hoisted five catch-and-shoot threes to compose 26.3% of his total field goals. Last season, he averaged just 3.4 per game to compose 15.9% of his total field goals, per NBA.com. Although Maxey netted only one of these attempts — he made 41.8% of them a year ago — his quality of looks throughout the contest was significantly better than the past three seasons and signaled a splendid scoring campaign ahead. With James and Jaylen Brown now flanking Maxey, Edgecombe and Joel Embiid, the Sixers are swimming in the deep end of star power, scoring outlets and championship expectations. They are all eyeing a deep playoff run that culminates in a title. Step one of their journey began Tuesday with an impressive victory inside the reigning champs’ palace. There’s plenty to glean from that performance, most of it positive, as should be the case after defeating a team as daunting and as healthy as the Knicks. So, what did game one teach us about the Sixers? Where do they currently stand? Where can they go? And what hurdles might they need to overcome along the way? The stage is set for Tyrese Maxey to be his best self Maxey’s uptick in spoonfed threes underscored how much easier and reshaped his scoring load should be this season. While he’s a tremendous player and offensive cog, on-ball creation, especially from a standstill, is not his ideal deployment. Yet the past three seasons — with scant surrounding perimeter creation and Embiid toggling in and out of the lineup — consistently stretched him too thin as he garnered usage for which he’s unqualified. Philadelphia’s revamped roster will alleviate that burden and let him boogie as one of the league’s foremost off-ball scorers. Maxey is now free to zip around screens, catch the ball on the move, knife through tilted defenses and leverage his speed and shooting without his size and limited vision disrupting those efforts as often. Since 2023-24, Maxey’s rate of assisted makes has been 43%, 37% and 45%, according to Cleaning the Glass. Tuesday, 67% of his field goals were assisted, including 71% of his 2-pointers. The latter number there is the starkest shift; last year, only 37.8% of his 2s were assisted, per NBA.com. Maxey seems likely to enjoy far more opportunities this season being coaxed downhill with help from others rather than being burdened with the task himself. That’s a major windfall for his game. He is still the focal point of the offense (his 26.6% usage rate narrowly trailed Embiid’s 27.4%) but the means to reach those ends are more favorable. He went 7-of-10 inside the arc and drew nine free throws. Even if he won’t shoot 70% on 2s moving forward, he will shoot better than 22% (2-of-9) from deep. Those extremes offset one another. With reps like these, Maxey is primed for a titanic scoring season: View Link The Sixers are lethal when they run. How often will they? Beyond his vast off-ball scoring exploits in the half-court, Maxey’s sterling offensive signature stems in part from his transition prowess. Year after year, Philadelphia is a considerably more efficient open-floor team when he’s on the court. With James and Brown joining him and Edgecombe, a quartet of transition tycoons now don Sixers red, white and blue. Ideally, they’ll tap into that and produce as many easy buckets as possible. When they did hit the runway Tuesday, they thrived. According to Cleaning the Glass, they averaged 1.8 points per transition possession. But their fast-break frequency was only 10% (league average was 15.4% last season). Now, the Knicks were well-organized setting up their defense to discourage early offense chances, which is a hallmark of this group’s resistance. They’ve ranked seventh or better in opponent transition rate every season since 2023-24. But I’m fascinated to monitor how often the Sixers mash the accelerator — they’ve sat outside the top 10 in transition frequency every year since 2021-22 — because the chemistry among Maxey, Brown and James was evident. When those dudes had opportunities, they were prompt and cohesive seizing them. View Link Is this defense here to stay? Most opponents the Sixers face this year will not be as talented or connected as New York’s. Teams will have lapses in judgment or let tired legs prevail, so Philadelphia can successfully dial up the tempo. But if the Sixers keep defending like they did Tuesday, the stops will pile up, especially against less dangerous offenses than the Knicks’, and they’ll enjoy plenty of running and gunning, if they so choose. Philadelphia held New York to a 98.0 defensive rating and 24-of-61 shooting (39.3%) inside the arc. That defensive rating would’ve been its seventh-best mark across the entire 2025-26 season and fourth-best against all playoff opponents. The Sixers were led by a domineering rim protection performance from Embiid, who looked quite nimble and comfortable in space. Cycling through drop coverage, trapping and hedging, he disrupted ball-handlers and still bothered big men when they received passes. He recorded three blocks, a feat he accomplished only five times combined in 2024-25 and 2025-26, including the playoffs. New York took 25.4% of its shots at the rim when he was on the floor and 41.9% of them when he sat, per databallr. Embiid operating like a premier interior anchor drastically elevates Philadelphia’s defensive ceiling. As Brunson probed inside the arc, Embiid allowed the Sixers’ help defenders to continually stay home (no lob threat was a boon, too) and suppress the Knicks’ 3-point volume. Just 33.3% of their field goals came beyond the arc, which would’ve tied for their ninth-lowest rate of 2025-26. View Link And tape like that is supported by numbers like these: That was a defensive performance from Joel Embiid that I wasn't sure he still had left in him. If it continues, if he can once again anchor a top-10 defense, that would make the Sixers truly scary. https://t.co/2ADorW4GRT pic.twitter.com/PNiLAzJpqk — Derek Bodner (@DerekBodnerNBA) October 21, 2026 Helping punctuate Embiid’s retrograde defensive showing was Brown, who did not serve as Brunson’s primary defender but wielded his size and discipline to frustrate the 2026 Finals MVP during his cameos. View Link While Embiid roamed off of Josh Hart much of the second half, James assumed the Karl-Anthony Towns assignment to reel in Towns as a shooter, driver and playmaker. James touts the strength and foot speed to tightly close out on Towns without worries of being steamrolled to the rim and was diligent about interfering with his passing windows. As a result, Towns tallied one assist to four turnovers, repeatedly struggling to find beneficial space against his weathered counterpart. LeBron did a good job last night of disrupting KAT's passing windows. He's got the strength and foot speed to tightly close out on him without fear of being bowled through downhill and really made it tough for KAT to create quality looks as a playmaker or scorer: pic.twitter.com/dmGRaLBrG3 — Jackson Frank (@jackfrank_jjf) October 21, 2026 Embiid, Brown and James may have spearheaded Philadelphia’s suffocating defense but the supporting cast of Maxey (three steals, three blocks), Edgecombe (one steal) and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (one block) all contributed to harmonic execution. The Sixers seamlessly switched off-ball actions — Brown, James, Maxey, Caldwell-Pope and Edgecombe all have some matchup versatility — communicated punctually to prevent mismatches, rotated to blot out lucrative openings and applied necessary physicality to divert the Knicks from traveling where they pleased. View Link The James-Embiid frontline was scrutinized much of the offseason as it pertained to Philadelphia’s defensive possibilities. One game against one opponent — whose style is plainly out there to scout since it hardly altered the roster — does not extinguish all concerns. But it would be hard for them to start a season more encouragingly than they did. The perimeter quartet bouncing around, talking, pointing and effectively navigating screens ensured it would result in a shiny outcome. Sustained attention to detail and movement skills like those from the entire rotation will quell many of the worries that surrounded Philadelphia over the summer. Jaylen Brown, fitting in After the gaudiest season of his career as he filled in for the injured Jayson Tatum to lead the Boston Celtics offensively, many (including me) wondered how Brown may assimilate to a star-infused Sixers roster that wouldn’t require such towering, centralized usage. In his debut Tuesday night, Brown (19 points on 7-of-14 shooting, eight rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block) reverted back to his early NBA days when he wasn’t an All-NBA wing and saw many of his chances as a cutter, quick-hitting driver and off-ball attacker/shooter. His 50 touches ranked fourth on the Sixers, down from 66.1 per game last year, and six of his seven field goals were assisted (85.7%, up from 36% last year). The lone unassisted bucket was a slaloming transition score. His imprint occurred organically and as a backseat to Maxey, Embiid and James. View Link Even Brown’s seven misfires were within the construct of the offense and never felt overbearing. He missed a corner three off a sideline-out-of-bounds set, couldn’t convert a rhythmic turnaround inside over the diminutive Jose Alvarado, was bested by a Deuce McBride strip/block in early offense, walked Landry Shamet under the rim before having a layup roll out, caught a grenade late in a disjointed possession, clanked an open pull-up jumper over Shamet and left a spot-up three short. Although Brown was traded in a one-for-one deal involving Paul George, James’ acquisition meant he was truly replacing Kelly Oubre Jr. in the starting unit. During Oubre’s three seasons as a Sixer, opposing defenses, including the Knicks, routinely ignored him on the weak-side to muck up happenings elsewhere, confident he didn’t brandish the offensive arsenal to truly punish that gambit. With Brown in his stead, New York’s helpers felt more conflicted, unsure of whether to abandon a highly talented scorer like Brown or let other highly talented scorers like Embiid and Maxey run amok. His mere existence granted fellow All-Stars single coverage inside and they capitalized; Philadelphia’s rim frequency was 35.3% with him on the floor and 4.5%(!!) without him, per databallr. View Link A singular game does not immediately dissolve all questions about Brown’s fit and offensive duties. But it does capture how naturally he can embrace a valuable, amended role to complement his new running mates when facing the caliber of team the Sixers expect to see this spring. This whole experiment is still a work in progress Despite the win and a dogged defensive game, there is considerable room to improve. The Sixers’ 106 points yielded a 103.0 offensive rating. Sure, shooting 27.5% (11-of-40) beyond the arc hurt. But they didn’t compensate with pristine interior scoring, making 26-of-49 (53.1%) of their 2-pointers. Embiid didn’t seem entirely comfortable with his perimeter-based deployment, attempting seven triples (two were late-clock heaves), and rarely rolled to the free-throw line, his most potent area on the floor. That’s not a new development and I imagine his decade-long series of lower-body injuries has him cautious to play in a crowd as often nowadays. New York often sat on those potential rolls as well, which likely influenced his decision to hover around the arc. Yet he and Philadelphia are a much more fluid, lethal attack when he’s confronting defenders at the nail rather than almost exclusively sitting beyond the 3-point line as a “spacer” (defenses don’t worry about him there), handoff hub and screener. He’s a notoriously slow starter offensively (four points, 1-of-9 shooting in the 2025-26 season opener; 2-of-11 in his 2024-25 debut) and migrated toward the midrange as last year progressed, so it’s totally plausible that occurs again. The Sixers should hope it does to reach their tantalizing offensive ceiling. James set a handful of empty-corner ball-screens for Maxey and hardly rolled with vigor out of them either. It stagnated the offense at times and left potential profits on the table. According to Synergy, he’s ranked in the 24th percentile (2025-26, 1.00 points per possession) and 21st percentile (2024-25, 0.98 PPP) the past two seasons as a roller, so such usage hasn’t entirely suited him lately; space was, however, there to attack and he did not. I understand he takes a bit of time to ramp up each year but his explosion, both vertically and horizontally, is greatly diminished from his prime (duh). I thought that subdued his aggression and am curious whether those habits evolve over the season to better elevate the offense. Theoretically, he and Maxey should kill on those empty-corner actions. The Sixers’ peak is contingent on their front-court recording more inspiring ball-screen reps than these and being more commanding interior presences than totaling 27 points on 7-of-28 shooting (41.7% true shooting). View Link Game one speed bumps for a bunch of players still navigating how to best interact with each other on the court is not reason for panic, let alone against such a high-level defense. Embiid will be a much more imposing force offensively in six weeks than he is today. James will better understand where he’s optimized as a half-court cog by Christmas than he does today. But they are nonetheless areas to address as Philadelphia builds toward title contention and discovers itself offensively. And hey, doing so while 1-0 with a nifty win like that in your backpocket ain’t too shabby.

stories.title: Walter Clayton Jr. player profile: Championship DNA, shot making and a swing worth taking
stories.summary: After a tough rookie season, Walter Clayton Jr. needs a spot to settle in and regain his form. It could happen in Dallas
stories.detailText: Mar 29, 2025; San Francisco, CA, USA; Florida Gators guard Walter Clayton Jr. (1) celebrates defeating the Texas Tech Red Raiders during the West Regional final of the 2025 NCAA tournament at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Mavericks made one final roster addition ahead of Wednesday’s season-opening 128-110 loss at the Houston Rockets , signing former Iona and Florida guard Walter Clayton Jr. to a two-way contract. Clayton Jr. rose to prominence before the 2025 NBA Draft in the NCAA Tournament, almost single-handedly carrying his Florida Gators through the clutch repeatedly. Whether it be in the Round of 32 against UConn, the unreal comeback against Texas Tech in the Elite Eight, or the heroics of the National Championship game against Houston, anytime Florida needed something, Clayton Jr. provided it. SAN ANTONIO, TEXAS – APRIL 07: Walter Clayton Jr. #1 of the Florida Gators celebrates after defeating the Houston Cougars in the National Championship of the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at the Alamodome on April 07, 2025 in San Antonio, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images You are probably saying to yourself “Self, Walter Clayton Jr. was drafted in 2025, I don’t care what he did in college. How did he play in the NBA last season?” The answer to that is a bit more complicated! Clayton was selected 18th overall in the 2025 Draft by the Utah Jazz. The Jazz were very much not interested in winning last season, so many of the looks he received were not placing him in the best position to succeed. When Utah made the trade to acquire Jaren Jackson Jr. from Memphis, the Grizzlies demanded that he be part of that package. He was, and thus he played the last 24 games of the season in Memphis. Memphis, obviously, also wasn’t very interested in winning, thus the looks for Clayton Jr. were difficult. However, Clayton did a much better job of assisting and getting others involved while playing for the Grizzlies, as he racked up nearly six dimes per contest. And to top it all off, Clayton was playing his best ball at the end of the regular season, shooting 50% from deep and 47% overall in the month of April. Walter Clayton Jr.: Dallas Maverick. We have signed @w1clayton to a two-way contract ✍️ #MFFL pic.twitter.com/EMlB4PKJnP — Dallas Mavericks (@dallasmavs) October 22, 2026 Of course, Memphis had a roster crunch this offseason, and after being left without a partner on the dance floor, were forced to cut bait. Now, after a very short waiting period after clearing waivers, the 2025 NCAA Tournament’s Most Outstanding Player joins forces with that tournament’s highest drafted player in Cooper Flagg. So, what can you look for with Clayton Jr. here in Dallas? Here’s a few things that tell his story as a player. Clayton Jr. is fearless You don’t have the courage to step up and hit these outrageous shots the way Clayton did if you don’t have some intestinal fortitude, and he’s got that in spades. At 6’2”, he has to be intentional about getting shots off on the outside, and also a very physical and crafty finisher. He’s shown that in the past, as per Yahoo! Sports, Clayton Jr. shot over 60% at the rim in his final year at Florida. While he’s struggled in the NBA at times with that, I think part of that is rookie lumps, while the other part is just simply the floor math being tilted against him. I’d love to get another look at that from him in Dallas. Shooting is a strength… I think Coming out of Florida, Clayton shot nearly 40% on spot-up 3-pointers and 37% on off-the-dribble attempts. For a college player, those are fantastic numbers. As mentioned above, Clayton also excelled at finishing at the cup. In the NBA, he has done none of those well. Last year, Clayton shot a combined 75-of-244 from deep across his two stops, good for just under 31%. He also was just 47% on two-pointers in the NBA, a number that should be better. Now, small samples across a rookie season in which he was traded and not set up for success should be taken with a hefty grain of salt. But, it would be great to see the bounce back this season. The playmaking has taken a step forward One of the issues coming into his rookie year was the lack of real playmaking pop from Clayton. At Florida, he showed some flashes, but there were some head-scratching turnovers and, frankly, I just don’t think he saw the floor well at times. You could kind of crowd him a bit and with his shorter stature, it forced some issues. Well, in Memphis to end the season, Clayton averaged over eight assists per 36 minutes , while keeping his turnovers down to around three. That’s really good work and a great sign for his future. Best and worst case outcome The best-case scenario for Clayton seems to be a Payton Pritchard- or Jordan Clarkson-type of star-in-their-role player. If he can continue to showcase the playmaking pop, perhaps he can reach those upper-tier outcomes and become a starter in this league. At worst, Clayton is probably out of the league after the year, but that really only happens if the shot continues to fall off, he doesn’t keep up the playmaking, and is just overwhelmed when on the ball. In reality, I do think Clayton is an NBA player. He needs a steady home and a system that can maximize what he does. At Florida, Todd Golden implored that group to run, drive-and-kick and press the defense. I think Clayton Jr. can find some of that in Dallas, and I hope he is able to make it stick.

stories.summary: Our hot takes.
stories.detailText: ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 21: Paolo Banchero #5 of the Orlando Magic argues with Jalen Johnson #1 of the Atlanta Hawks at the end of the game at Kia Center on October 21, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the fourth of a series of roundtable questions I’m asking the staff here at Peachtree Hoops about the Hawks this upcoming season. The fourth question: what is your boldest ta ke for the Hawks in 2026-27? Wes: Despite the NBA being an incredibly difficult adjustment for rookie guards, I predict Kingston Flemings both makes the All-Rookie First Team and finds his way into the starting lineup by the end of the season. Throughout preseason, he already looks the part of a chiseled veteran guard, getting after it on defense and protecting the ball with a pristine assist-to-turnover ratio. It’s rare for Kelvin Sampson to trust a freshman guard to run the show at Houston, but Flemings stepped in immediately and did just that. Why can’t he do the same for Quin Snyder and the Hawks this season? Malik: My boldest take for the season is that the Hawks finish as a top-2 seed in the Eastern Conference. This team feels like they can do something similar to what the Detroit Pistons did the last two years, where they made the playoffs (and ironically played the Knicks) and then the following year was the No. 1 seed in the East. The Hawks brought back their core and made some key additions that will make them a better team. If Jalen Johnson and others like Dyson Daniels can take another step in their game, the Hawks could (boldly) be a team to be reckoned with this season. Garrett: The Hawks will finish as a top five defensive team, and Jalen Johnson will finish in the top five in MVP voting. I’m buying into the combination of Daniels, Alexander-Walker and Dort on the perimeter. Atlanta has the personnel to make opponents work for everything, and I expect that to become this team’s identity. The challenge is bringing that effort consistently, but I think this group can do it. As for Johnson, I think that defensive support helps him take another leap. Having Dort available to handle tough assignments should allow Johnson to put more energy into leading the offense. He’ll still have responsibilities on both ends, but he doesn’t have to carry every burden himself. If he builds on his scoring and playmaking while leading Atlanta to a strong playoff seed, I believe he’ll give voters a reason to put his name in that top five conversation. Graham: The Hawks will be the NBA’s best defensive team this season. The Hawks have so many defensive options now up and down the roster, so much versatility to play with. They have the option to put out the defensive lineup of Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Lu Dort, Jalen Johnson, and Onyeka Okongwu on the court. However, this NBA leading defense is only possible if Jalen Johnson buys back into defense (which has never looked the same since his increased offensive role two seasons ago), the Hawks will lead the league in defensive rating. When he’s engaged on that end, Johnson is a very good defender, and if the Hawks are to contend he has to buy back in defensively.

stories.title: Steve Kerr caught blasting ‘bulls–t’ Lakers favoritism on hot mic in Warriors loss
stories.summary: Warriors coach Steve Kerr was caught on a hot mic criticizing officials for favoring the Los Angeles Lakers during Golden State's 127-105 season-opening loss.
stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors Head Coach Steve Kerr believes the Los Angeles Lakers received a favorable whistle during Wednesday night’s NBA season opener — and was caught saying as much on a hot mic. During the third quarter of the Lakers’ 127–105 win over Kerr’s Warriors, the legendary coach pulled rookie Yaxel Lendeborg aside as he checked out of the game and told him, “[It’s] the bulls–t in the NBA. They call all that s–t here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena,” which was audible on ESPN’s broadcast. A clip of Kerr saying this to Lendeborg quickly went viral on social media, and already had over 450,000 views in about 11 hours. Golden State Warriors Head Coach Steve Kerr thinks the Lakers received a favorable whistle during Wednesday’s game. AP Photo/Ali Gradischer Steve Kerr CALLED OUT the Lakers whistle on the hot mic: "They call all that sh*t here, they wouldn't call it in any other arena." pic.twitter.com/FjGzYPdqg9 — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) October 22, 2026 The stats don’t back up Kerr’s sentiment, as the Lakers actually had more fouls called on then (25) than the Warriors did (19). The two teams also both shot 27 free throws. However, many who watched the game on Wednesday felt like some fouls that the Lakers received were questionable, so those stats don’t tell the entire story. Lakers superstar guard Luka Dončić was the subject of Kerr’s frustration. NBAE via Getty Images Warriors star Steph Curry warms up at Crypto Arena before the season opener in LA. London Entertainment Lakers superstar guard Luka Dončić was the subject of Kerr’s frustration, as Lendeborg spent much of the game matched up on him. Dončić had nine of the Lakers’ 27 free throws and finished with a game-high 28 points in the victory. Kerr’s gripe seems to be that the Lakers playing at home is what led to their favorable whistle. In that case, maybe Golden State will get a better whistle when they play the Memphis Grizzlies at home tomorrow night. stories.title: Lakers encouraged by status of key player’s injury after scary moment
stories.summary: The biggest hiccup for the Lakers during a night that didn’t feature many of them was a scary injury involving a key player on the roster.
stories.detailText: The Lakers’ season-opening win over the Warriors to kick off the franchise’s Luka Doncic era went about as well as could’ve been expected. Doncic, in addition to Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves, dominated the team’s in-state rival, with the Lakers’ “Big 3” combining for 77 points, 21 rebounds, 14 assists, five steals and three blocked shots. The “nasty” defense Kessler spoke about showed up in the middle two quarters, with the Warriors combining for just 35 points in the second and third periods after the Lakers allowed 33 points in the first. The biggest hiccup for the Lakers during a night that didn’t feature many of them: A scary injury moment involving a key player on the roster. Jake LaRavia (12) was having a strong season opener before leaving with an injury. NBAE via Getty Images Midway through the fourth, with the Lakers up by 33 points, Jake LaRavia attempted to drive into the paint with LJ Cryer guarding him. Cryer impeded the drive, with the 2022 first-round draft pick awkwardly twisting his right ankle/lower leg before hobbling and falling to the floor. LaRavia laid on the court and writhed in pain before team trainers helped him back to the bench. Jake LaRavia (12) of the Los Angeles Lakers arrives to the arena before a game. NBAE via Getty Images He was able to put weight on the leg before going back to the locker room after subbing out of the game. While coach JJ Redick didn’t have an update on LaRavia immediately after the game, he was encouraged about his status compared to how it felt in the immediate aftermath of the injury. “I’m probably more positive than when it first happened,” Redick said. “But again. he’ll be evaluated. And the next time I talk to you guys, we’ll have an update.” Jake LaRavia’s impressive preseason carried over into the regular season. NBAE via Getty Images LaRavia was having a strong game before going down with the injury, scoring 10 points on 4 of 5 shooting off of the bench. “I saw him being himself,” Redick said. “Again when he is shooting with confidence and making catch-and-shoot 3s, that’s an added bonus. We have a group of guys that do a lot of things to impact winning that don’t necessarily show up in the box score, certainly won’t show up in a highlight reel on Instagram. He’s a winning player.”

teamStories.summary: The Spurs are tied for last place with a bunch of bad teams. Other winless teams the Spurs are tied with include the Bulls, Bucks, Nets, Pelicans, Suns and Kings. Not a group to be associated with. The Spurs are also tied with the “world champion New York Knicks”. Feels odd to write those words after […]
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - OCTOBER 20: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs looks on during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on October 20, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Spurs are tied for last place with a bunch of bad teams. Other winless teams the Spurs are tied with include the Bulls, Bucks, Nets, Pelicans, Suns and Kings. Not a group to be associated with. The Spurs are also tied with the “world champion New York Knicks”. Feels odd to write those words after 53 years. And because of Tuesday’s night’s game, the Spurs main rival is undefeated on the season. And yes, the Spurs’ best player had a dreadful offensive game against the Thunder. Near the end of the second quarter, I asked my friend who was watching the game with me, “Does Victor have a basket yet?” The answer was “no”. And he didn’t actually make a “shot” all night – his one basket came in the second half on a dunk off a lob pass. And yes, the Spurs second-longest tenured player, Devin Vassell, scored only 7 points in 31 minutes, on 25% shooting. Perhaps being forced to defend OKC bigs like Holmgren on the other end was a bit draining? And yes, the Thunder’s best player had a great offensive game. I was surprised to see that the box score had SGA at only 13 for 27 from the floor. It felt like he didn’t miss any. It also felt like a bunch of shots were punctuated with “and one!” Which always sucks. And yes, the Thunder’s bigs looked pretty good. Punching bag Chet Holmgren outscored Victor Wembanyama 14-12 and blocked his shot at least once, looking not at all like the cowering Chet from last season’s WC Finals. And the Thunder new kid, Aday Mara, played a very effective 12 minutes, making three times as many shots as Victor, and doing something never before seen: blocking a lob-dunk by our Frenchman. The Spanish dude might be a problem going forward. And the Thunder defense looked very strong, not missing Lu Dort at all. Alex Caruso was his usual pesky self on D and also nailed both of this three-pointers. SGA was also great on D, getting three steals and three blocks – he is clearly ahead in the MVP race thus far in the season. (Though Anthony Edwards may want a word.) Based on all of that, the consensus among the media, and presumably everyone who watched the game, is that the Thunder dominated the Spurs, “They just wanted it more”. An understandable conclusion, especially because of how the Thunder ended last season, having to watch the young Spurs emotionally celebrate after Game Seven of the Western Conference Finals on their own floor. And then hearing about it all summer. I agreed with the consensus until I calmed down and looked at the box score, as coaches (and former coaches) like to do. When I look at the box score, I first look at extra possessions by each team – turnovers and offensive rebounds. The Spurs had two more turnovers (13-11) and the same number of offensive rebounds (10). OKC took two more shots from the field, but the Spurs shot five more free throws. The Spurs also shot a bit better on those free throws – 88% t0 80%. On two-point shots, the Spurs shot better – 26-56 as opposed the Thunder’s 27-64. The Spurs also took more threes, 37-31. You can see where this is going. OKC won the game by 12 points because they shot significantly better on threes. They made four more threes than the Spurs on six less attempts. I checked my math with AI, and confirmed that four more three pointers equals 12 more points – the margin of victory in the game. OKC outshot the Spurs from three largely because Jared McCain came off the bench to go 6-8 from three, with Caruso chipping in his two. If McCain shoots his career average, he only makes three three-pointers, not six. If Caruso misses one of his two, he is still at 50%. And if both of those things happen, OKC has 12 less points, the margin of victory in Game One of Eighty-Two. Not coincidentally, McCain was a game-high plus 20 in his 22 minutes, Caruso plus 16 in his 25 minutes. All in all, despite the final score, with everything that went wrong for the Spurs and everything that went right for the Thunder, the game was actually quite even. So after carefully analyzing the box score, I felt a bit better about Tuesday night. And then I looked at the Knicks-76ers box score, and felt worse again. Jalen Brunson shot 6-19 from the floor after seemingly making all his shots against the Spurs in the Finals. OG Anunoby went 1-10 from three, after shooting a bazillion percent from three (actually 50%) in the Finals. Now I am unhappy again. Stupid box scores.

The good guys will wear silver in 19 games; 11 will feature their second-year silver jersey with the “San Antonio” wordmark (Statement Edition) while eight will feature the new Classic Edition throwbacks . Both sets will appear at the Frost Bank Center five times. The Spurs will don their fan-favorite “Fiesta” jerseys (City Edition) for 13 games, with six of those at home. The most noteworthy jersey quirk on the schedule involves that City Edition set. We won’t see the Fiesta jerseys until after the New Year, but they’ll be featured 13 times in a 39-game stretch. The Spurs will be in white for their Paris game against the Pelicans three days later. stories.title: Barring setbacks, Bucs QB Baker Mayfield expected to start vs. Panthers
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield expects to return from a thumb injury, barring any setbacks, and play when the Buccaneers face the Panthers on Sunday.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, Fla. -- Barring any setbacks, the expectation is that Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield will return Sunday after a three-week absence due to a dislocated right thumb suffered in Week 3. The Bucs, currently sitting at 1-5, begin divisional play at the Carolina Panthers (3-2). Mayfield was a full participant in Wednesday's and Thursday's practices and the Bucs' communications staff even delayed its weekly quarterback media availability from Wednesday to Thursday to get a better sense of the team's direction. That's when Mayfield walked in, speaking publicly for the first time since suffering the injury. Mayfield said he felt "very confident" in his ability to grip the ball and that while there was some degree of tendon and ligament damage, he believes that with rest and giving the wound time to heal (he did not undergo surgery but the dislocation created a wound that required stitches) he has "gotten to a place where it's strong enough to be able to play" and "feels good." Mayfield has been practicing with a specially made glove on his right hand that has a pad on the back side of the thumb to protect it from bending backward again. It contains metal for reinforcement. "I mean, truly when you're throwing with a glove, you got to get used to it. Just changing your release points. Can't grip it as hard because it'll stick to the glove. Different things like that. So just getting a lot of reps, getting practice with it, getting used to it and it feels fine." The team's equipment staff sought out the Tampa Bay Rays for help as it was something the Rays had done previously for an athlete. They went through different options until Mayfield found something he was comfortable with. He said that after the initial adjustment, he doesn't feel a difference in it. "It's just like me wearing a glove," he said. Mayfield said the big concern for him was the impact of the ball from under center with Graham Barton . "It feels fine gripping it, throwing it," Mayfield said. "It's just that the impact stuff, that was really what my concern was and it's felt great so far." Barton said that's really a matter of him being as consistent as possible. "You want to place it firmly in between his hands so if anything's off and it hits his thumb -- I can imagine that early on is something you think about just in the back of your head," Barton said. "But I think we've had great exchanges this week. And there haven't really been any issues. "Baker's a fearless competitor and I think that stuff, when we get to Sunday, we'll be back to normal. That can be weird for a quarterback, especially on his throwing hand, but I think if anyone can handle it well, it'll be him. The initial prognosis was a three-week minimum, but Mayfield said he tried to beat that and was aiming for the Pittsburgh Steelers last week. But he wasn't 100% and felt backup Jalon Daniels gave the team a better chance to win. He acknowledged that at 1-5 they have a steep hill to climb as they enter divisional play. But with only the Panthers holding a winning record, they're not out of it. "It is," Mayfield said. "Got to take it one game at a time. And our opponent this week is the one leading division, and so we got to take care of business this week and that's all that matters. It's going to be a 'one game at a time' mentality. But listen -- our guys are ready for it and we'll see what happens." Despite his absence, Mayfield has been very involved over the past three weeks, doing everything he could to help Daniels in meetings, serving as an "extra voice" for him, and coaching him up in between series in practice and on the sideline in games. He offered input to offensive coordinator Zac Robinson on what he thought could best set Daniels up for success. "I got to say this, I'm really proud of Jalon," Mayfield said. "I thought, thrown into the fire there, three starts in a row, got a win on the second one in prime time, which was huge. Just the guy he is, the progression he's had from spring through training camp to now -- he's grown up a ton. It was really fun to watch. I know he wants some plays back, but that's the evolution of quarterback. When you're thrown into fire like that, he handled it well." The feeling in the locker room is that the team was able to make progress with Daniels that will help them better be able to support Mayfield. Coach Todd Bowles said that he believes the mental reps helped Mayfield as well. "I feel like he's been intact and hands on with everything still, rather it's coaching the guys up in practice in the spots to be on the field and just how to be detailed and be better for Jalon and his situation," wide receiver Ted Hurst III said. "And now he's making his return and we're definitely behind him and he's back to the normal, I'll say." The team also had what was described by Robinson, Mayfield and several players as a tough meeting earlier this week to address a struggling passing game and the need to be more detailed and consistent with timing and landmarks -- something Mayfield supported. "We needed to have it," Mayfield said. "It's one of those things -- it's uncomfortable. You can't be sensitive in that. Everybody's got a hand in it. It wasn't just about the last game. It was really more so talking about everything that we've done wrong."

stories.title: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet activated off PUP list
stories.summary: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet, who has yet to play this season after scoring 12 TDs in 2025, has been activated off the PUP list and added to the 53-man roster.
stories.detailText: RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks activated running back Zach Charbonnet off the physically unable to perform list Thursday, an expected move amid his comeback from a torn ACL. It's not certain that Charbonnet, who is only eight months removed from surgery, will make his season debut Sunday night when the Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs at Lumen Field. Coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that it's a "possibility" that he plays "in some capacity." "Just taking it a day at a time," Charbonnet said Thursday in his first comments to reporters since he was injured in January. "But whenever I'm out there, it's going to be special and I'm just going to be happy to get back out there." The Seahawks on Thursday also placed second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve. A source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Arroyo, a 2025 second-round pick who caught one pass for 17 yards in six games this season, is having season-ending surgery to repair a shoulder injury he suffered last week in a loss to the Denver Broncos . The Seahawks listed Charbonnet as a full participant in practice Wednesday. He had been listed as limited on the first eight injury reports released by the team since it designated him to return to practice Oct. 1. Thursday marked the 21-day deadline to move Charbonnet to the 53-man roster. In a co-starting role last season alongside Kenneth Walker III , Charbonnet rushed for 730 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. He tore his left ACL in Seattle's divisional-round win over the San Francisco 49ers on Jan. 17 and had surgery Feb. 12. Charbonnet said this was "around" the time that he was aiming to return. "I'm feeling pretty good," Charbonnet said. "Just going a day at a time. Seeing how it adapts with picking up practice and stuff like that." With Charbonnet beginning the season on PUP and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price missing the last three games with a chest injury, Seattle is averaging 107.2 rushing yards per game and 3.9 yards per carry, both of which rank 18th. Their backfield trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have combined to lose four fumbles. Price, who was placed on IR in Week 4, has to miss at least one more game.

stories.title: Ravens' Humphrey expresses displeasure over 'slander' against QB Jackson
stories.summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey voiced his displeasure over what he called "slander" against quarterback Lamar Jackson.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey voiced his displeasure over what he called "slander" against quarterback Lamar Jackson . On Thursday, Humphrey went on a tangent after being asked how Jackson looked at practice. Jackson returned to the field this week after missing the last two games with a left ankle injury. "It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Humphrey said. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles. I'm in the hot tub and it's this, that and the third. Unfair treatment." Humphrey was asked if he was referring to injury "slander," but he didn't clarify. Humphrey then said, "I just feel like sometimes it seems like it gets away from ... I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. But I do know this, if Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play, and that's kind of all I can say for that." When asked again exactly what he meant, Humphrey replied, "Whatever I said is whatever I said. You can take it however you want." Jackson, who sprained his ankle 18 days ago, moved around well at Thursday's practice. He participated in every drill during the media viewing portion. He was listed as a limited participant for the second straight day. Before bringing up the "slander" against Jackson, Humphrey was initially asked about how Jackson looked at practice. "I think anything relating to Lamar is the thing that I don't talk about," Humphrey said. "I think the only one that really does talk about [Lamar] is Lamar. I think if Lamar can play, it'd be great. If he doesn't, we got Snoop [backup Tyler Huntley ]." If Jackson can play Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals , it would be a timely return. Jackson is 11-2 in his career against the Bengals, throwing 24 touchdowns against six interceptions.

stories.title: Giants committed to helping quarterback J.J. McCarthy 'do what he does best' in Week 7 start
stories.summary: The Giants will be using a third different starting quarterback this season when they travel to Houston to take on the Texans on Sunday afternoon after announcing earlier in the week that J.J. McCarthy earned the start over Jameis Winston.
stories.detailText: The Giants will be using a third different starting quarterback this season when they travel to Houston to take on the Texans on Sunday afternoon after announcing earlier in the week that J.J. McCarthy earned the start over Jameis Winston . How long of a leash New York will give McCarthy remains to be seen , but it stands to reason the 23-year-old will get a good look for the foreseeable future considering the Giants went out and traded for him four weeks ago following Jaxson Dart ’s knee injury – not to mention his fourth-quarter performance against the New Orleans Saints which nearly resulted in a wild comeback in a game that was started by Winston. So, after four weeks of familiarizing himself with the offense, it appears McCarthy is now ready to lead the Giants. “We've been working for four weeks now trying to get him to learn this whole offense and not just learn packages, and that's been his biggest challenge,” said offensive coordinator Matt Nagy . “Now here we are, and he gets an opportunity to be in this spot, and so it's our job now as coaches to make sure that we're helping him do what he does best.” McCarthy’s first start for New York will come in a difficult environment: on the road against a Texans team that has won two straight after an 0-4 start with a defense that can pressure the quarterback, including 18 sacks this season. In fact, defensive end Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. To his credit, McCarthy, like Dart, has the ability to run the ball and may need to show off his legs and evade some defenders on Sunday with the Giants having allowed 18 sacks this season. Of course, most of that has been with Winston under center. “We're going into an environment where it's going to be loud on the road against a tough defense that likes to play fast, so we've got to keep all that in perspective,” Nagy said. “But at the same point in time, our guys are hungry and ready to go.” McCarthy’s dual threat at quarterback is something New York will likely utilize in its attempt to optimize the quarterback’s skillset, especially with the running backs struggling to move the ball efficiently at the moment. It even opens the door for more play calls that the Giants initially trained for with Dart that they weren’t equipped to do with Winston. Regardless of what the game plan is, McCarthy is prepared to execute it just like he did in limited action with little preparation last Sunday which impressed New York. Hopefully with a full week of practice as the starter, it will only help the youngster. “His operation was really good in that stressful time in that moment,” Nagy said about McCarthy in regards to the fourth quarter. “We were playing a little bit of hurry up. There's a lot of communication that goes on, and there's, quite honestly, even in that moment in some of our no-huddle, end-of-game situational stuff, that he has had zero reps at just because of time and practice. “So balancing all that, I thought he did that really well, but now we've got to be able to say, hey, listen, this is now a full week of a real game plan, and we cannot make it difficult on him. We've got to make sure we're doing what he does well.” Having players like wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely as targets all game will surely help in making it easier for McCarthy who threw for 243 yards on 11 completions after entering the game against the Saints. That kind of stat line may not exactly translate against the Texans, but the Giants are excited, regardless, with how the quarterback looked on the field (and during practice) and the decisions he was making. “The operation right now, what he's doing is amazing,” Nagy said. “Then you throw in some of the throws that he made, not just when we're 70 yards away, but when we're in that red zone or when we're in a situation where you've got to make a throw. He did that, too. His demeanor has been really good for all four weeks. He's very eager to learn. He wants as much as he can get to digest within our offense. “It's our job now, what we've been trying to do is just see what can he handle? And now as we go into that this week, it's like, OK, this is what we think he can handle, but how do we get that to a point of being able to do what our guys do well, too, on offense, the players. Because, again, you're going to a guy who, whether you like it or not, just hasn't had reps with these other players on our offense.”

stories.title: Seahawks activate RB Zach Charbonnet from PUP list before facing Chiefs, Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III
stories.summary: Walker has outrushed Seattle by himself, leading the NFL in rushing yards with Kansas City.
stories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks’ rushing attack could get some major help for Week 7’s matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Running back Zach Charbonnet was activated from the physically unable to perform list, the team announced on Thursday . He has not played this season due to a torn ACL he sustained during a divisional playoff game versus the San Francisco 49ers in January. The Seahawks go into Sunday’s game with the 14th-ranked rushing attack in the NFL at 643 yards in six games. That number might especially sting when considering that Kenneth Walker III has outrushed Seattle by himself with 665 yards in one fewer game, leading the NFL in that category. Walker earned Super Bowl MVP honors for the Seahawks last season with 131 rushing yards in the 29-13 win over the New England Patriots. But he went on to sign with the Chiefs as a free agent and has changed Kansas City’s offense to more of a power-running attack. Emanuel Wilson leads the Seahawks in rushing so far this season with 303 yards and 2 touchdowns on 87 carries. Rookie Jadarian Price (119 yards) was Seattle’s starter, but has been sidelined for the past three weeks with a chest injury . He is eligible to return from injured reserve next week. George Holani has 97 yards on 31 carries. Activating Charbonnet does not guarantee that he will play on Sunday, though head coach Mike Macdonald sounded optimistic that the fourth-year back would get carries after being a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. "Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting, and there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that's exciting," Macdonald said to John Boyle of the Seahawks’ official site on Monday. Charbonnet had to activate him off the PUP list after opening his 21-day practice window on Oct. 1. If he hadn’t been added back to the active 53-man roster, Charbonnet would have had to sit out the remainder of the season, under NFL rules.

stories.title: Bengals vs. Ravens Injury Report: Lamar Jackson limited again
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson remains a major question mark for Week 7.
stories.detailText: The Cincinnati Bengals are looking good on the injury front as they prepare for a big AFC North clash with the Baltimore Ravens. On the other side, Baltimore may have a chance to get their franchise quarterback back on the field, according to Thursday’s reporting. For the Bengals, safety Kyle Dugger (quad) was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday. It is unknown whether he will play on Sunday, but he appears to be trending toward a return after being out since Week 3. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill both got a veteran’s rest day. For Baltimore, quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) was listed as a limited participant Thursday. On Wednesday, he was listed as limited as well, but it sounds like he got a decent amount more work done in Thursday’s practice. Media members reported Jackson was active in practice and wasn’t seen favoring the ankle that has kept him out of the lineup since October 4th. stories.title: The Seahawks prepare to face former teammate Kenneth Walker III while Zack Charbonnet could return
stories.summary: As the Seahawks prepare to face former teammate Kenneth Walker III, they may be getting some help with their own running game.
stories.detailText: As the Seahawks prepare to face former teammate Kenneth Walker III , they may be getting some help with their own running game. Seahawks running back Zack Charbonnet may play for the first time this season Sunday when Seattle hosts the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs . He participated in a full practice Wednesday and was placed on the active roster Thursday. His return couldn't come at a better time for the Seahawks, who are coming off a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos last Thursday night. It was the third loss this season for the defending Super Bowl champions. The Seahawks' run game has struggled for much of the season and they could use Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in January and spent the first six games of the season on the physically unable to perform list. "There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said this week. Seattle is ranked 18th in the league with an average of 107.2 total yards on the ground this season. They have five rushing touchdowns. Rookie Jadarian Price , who was expected to help, is out with a chest/shoulder injury. Charbonnet rushed for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns for the Seahawks last season before he was injured. Of course, one of the reasons why Seattle's run game has dipped this season is the loss of Walker, their Super Bowl MVP who went to the Chiefs as a free agent in the offseason "But I think there’s mixed emotions. We’re happy for him, but also, we’re trying to figure out ways to stop this guy, too," Macdonald said. Walker rushed for 128 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. It was the fourth game he's topped 100 yards rushing this season. Walker is averaging a league-leading 133 yards rushing per game and has run for eight touchdowns so far. Walker became the Seahawks' top back after Charbonnet was injured, and ran for 135 yards in the Super Bowl against the Patriots to earn MVP honors. Chiefs coach Andy Reid expects Walker to treat his return to Seattle like he does every game. “I think the boys there will try to get after him a little bit. But he’s a pretty level-headed guy. The way he plays, you’re going to get a good rep when he gets the ball in his hands,” Reid said. "He kind of has one speed: He’s coming at you. It doesn’t matter who he’s playing or where he’s playing.” The Seahawks' run defense is allowing an average of 96 yards a game, with four total rushing touchdowns. Seattle has not allowed a rusher to go 100 or more yards in 35 straight games, the league's longest current streak. Need to know Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) at the Seattle Seahawks (3-3) When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. EDT, NBC. Latest odds: Seattle by 2 1/2 points. Against the spread: Chiefs 3-2, Seahawks 2-4. Last week: The Chiefs beat the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6, the Seahawks fell to the Denver Broncos 17-14. Last meeting: Kansas City won 24-10 on Dec. 24, 2022, at Arrowhead. Series record: Kansas City leads 34-19. Matchup to watch Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes against the Seahawks' pass defense. Mahomes has thrown for 1,309 yards with nine touchdowns and three interceptions. He's completing 66.5% of his passes. But he may be challenged by Seattle, which ranks atop the NFL allowing just 141.3 passing yards per game, and only eight total passing touchdowns. In his two career games against the Seahawks, Mahomes has thrown for 497 yards with six touchdowns. Stats and stuff — The victory over the Chargers was quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 100th career regular-season victory. — The Chiefs sacked Chargers QB Justin Herbert four times. They were the first sacks for the defense in three games. — TE Travis Kelce has a reception in 196 consecutive games, longest active streak in the league. — WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba has five games with 100 or more receiving yards this season. He leads the league with 717 receiving yards, seven touchdowns and an average of 119.5 yards per game. He also leads the NFL with 17 100-yard games since 2024. — The Chiefs lead the league with an average of 414 yards in total offense per game. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Morris returns to Atlanta and is expected to have 49ers defense try to pressure Falcons QB Penix
stories.summary: — Raheem Morris, part of the Atlanta Falcons' leadership team that made Michael Penix Jr. the No. 8 overall pick in the 2024 draft, will return to Atlanta on Sunday as the defensive coordinator of an undefeated San Francisco 49ers team that will try...
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- — Raheem Morris, part of the Atlanta Falcons ' leadership team that made Michael Penix Jr . the No. 8 overall pick in the 2024 draft, will return to Atlanta on Sunday as the defensive coordinator of an undefeated San Francisco 49ers team that will try to give the third-year quarterback and the Falcons their third straight loss. Morris, who was 16-18 in two seasons as the Falcons head coach, and general manager Terry Fontenot were fired on Jan. 5 following an 8-9 finish in 2025. It was Atlanta's eighth consecutive losing season. Morris, who was popular with Falcons players, likely will receive warm greetings in his return to Atlanta. His defense can be expected to try to make things uncomfortable for Penix as the 49ers (6-0) try to remain undefeated while the Falcons (2-4) look to end an ugly two-game losing streak. “It’s going to be exciting,” Penix said. "It’s going to be good to be able to see him again, but we got to find a way to obviously put points on the board against his defense.” Penix is 2-2 as a starter this season and 6-10 overall. Penix was sacked five times and fumbled twice, losing one, in last week's 31-23 loss to Chicago. Penix struggled against the Bears' defensive pressure as the Falcons trailed 14-0 before getting a first down and 31-7 before finally finding momentum while running their two-minute offense in the final quarter. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said he knows the 49ers defense will want to win for Morris. “I don’t think they can be more motivated," Shanahan said. "I think our guys are as motivated as you can get each week. I don’t think they get too caught up in that stuff, but I know they care about Raheem a lot and definitely would want to do that for him. But, I don’t think we’re looking at too much of a personal game like that.” Penix left a 30-23 overtime loss to Baltimore on Oct 11 in the fourth quarter with a rib injury . He missed the first two games this season while completing his recovery from ACL surgery on his left knee. He has had no setbacks with his surgically repaired knee but he has been sacked nine times in four games. Coach Kevin Stefanski said “this league can be a copycat league” so he knows Morris and the 49ers will take note of the Bears' success in pressuring Penix. Penix said a key will be avoiding obvious passing situations on third down. “We’ve just got to be dominant on those early downs ... and got to be great in our execution,” Penix said. “All the small details, whatever it is that we haven’t been doing right these last couple games, and just figuring that out and get back to playing our football.” Need to know San Francisco (6-0) at Atlanta (2-4). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox. Latest odds: 49ers by 2 1/2. Against the spread: 49ers 4-2; Falcons 2-4. Last week: 49ers beat Washington 23-17; Falcons lost to Chicago 31-23. Last meeting: 49ers beat Falcons 20-10 on Oct. 19, 2025, in San Francisco. Series record: 49ers lead 49-33-1. Matchup to watch 49ers left defensive end Keion White and left defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa vs. Falcons right tackle Jawaan Taylor and right guard Chris Lindstrom . White leads the 49ers with 3 1/2 sacks and Odighizuwa has three sacks. If the 49ers take notes from the Bears' winning defensive game plan last week, they also can be expected to utilize blitzes to put pressure on Penix, but the Falcons' hopes of keeping Penix on his feet will start with blocking the left side of the defensive front. Stats and stuff — The 49ers are 6-0 for the fourth time since joining the NFL in 1950. They only times they started 7-0 or better came in 2019 and 1990. — San Francisco has at least four sacks in back-to-back games for the first time since doing it three straight games in 2023. The Niners have 15 sacks already this season after having a league-low 20 in 2025. — Niners quarterback Brock Purdy is one of two quarterbacks in NFL history to open a season 6-0 with at least 15 total touchdowns rushing and passing and two or fewer turnovers. Tom Brady also did it in 2015. — George Kittle has TD catches in four of the past five games and is tied for the league lead for tight ends with five TDs on the season. Kittle’s 30 TD catches on passes from Purdy are tied for the most of any QB-TE combo in 49ers history with Alex Smith and Vernon Davis. — Niners kicker Eddy Pineiro has missed three PATs and three FGs this season for a league-worst six missed kicks. He missed only five last season. — The Falcons earned a 28-14 win over the 49ers in 2022, the most recent time the teams played in Atlanta. — Falcons running back Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 758 scrimmage yards. He ranks second with 641 rushing yards. — Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts has a combined three touchdown catches in the past two games, including two last week. — Defensive end Za'Darius Smith has 3 1/2 sacks in his first five games with Atlanta. — Veteran quarterback Andy Dalton , who signed with Atlanta on Monday, is expected to be the emergency third quarterback behind Penix and Tua Tagovailoa . Cooper Rush was released. — Stefanski said he will stick with rookie Zachariah Branch as a return specialist after Branch lost two fumbles against the Bears, one on a fumbled fair catch on a punt and one on a kickoff return. ------ AP Pro Football Writer Josh Dubow contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
