stories.title: Chiefs place LT Josh Simmons on IR as rehab process stalls
stories.summary: The Chiefs have placed left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, further delaying his return from a bulging disk in his lower back.
stories.detailText: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Kansas City Chiefs placed left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve Thursday, further delaying his return from a bulging, herniated disk in his lower back. After being a limited participant in the Chiefs' three practices last week, Simmons still felt pain in his back and left leg, the same leg he had previously suffered a torn patellar tendon in back in October 2024 while playing for Ohio State . Head trainer Rick Burkholder shared Thursday that Simmons reported feeling discomfort in his left calf following a training camp practice Aug. 17, prompting the team to order an MRI, which revealed a "bulging, herniated" disk, he said. "That disk problem was higher up than what we normally see in most of our offensive linemen, which complicated the case," Burkholder said of Simmons. "The repeat MRI, a few weeks later, showed that the disk had improved, so no surgery was recommended. Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day. However, we feel he has plateaued in the rehab process. He's just not there yet." Burkholder then explained that Simmons took the rest of Wednesday afternoon off to discuss the next steps of his treatment with his family and his representative, thus the "personal" and "back" designations on the Chiefs' injury report. According to Burkholder, "everybody" agreed that Simmons needed to be placed on injured reserve, a move that will force the lineman to miss at least the next four games -- against Seattle , Denver , the New York Jets and Atlanta . The earliest Simmons can return is Week 11, when the Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 22. The team and Simmons are still determining how and where he will continue his rehab. "I give a lot of credit to Josh, my physicians and my staff for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended," Burkholder added. "He just needs more time to return to full function." Simmons' absence has opened the door for undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson , who played right tackle in college for the Indiana Hoosiers . Benson is the first undrafted offensive rookie to start in Week 1 for Andy Reid during his entire 14-year coaching tenure in Kansas City. Benson has done a commendable job as the lineman most responsible for protecting the blind side of quarterback Patrick Mahomes , earning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month in September. On the other side, right tackle Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, is currently in the NFL's concussion protocol. Joshua Ezeudu , who joined the Chiefs in late August via a trade with the New York Giants , is expected to start in Moore's place in Sunday night's road game against the Seahawks. Since selecting Simmons in the first round of the 2025 NFL draft, the Chiefs have played more games without him (14) than with him (eight). The last time Simmons played was last year on Thanksgiving Day, when the team fell to the Dallas Cowboys . During that game, Simmons suffered a dislocated and fractured left wrist , a season-ending injury that required surgery. Before that setback, Simmons was an emerging rookie, as he allowed a pressure rate of just 6.6%, which at the time was the third-lowest mark among left tackles and the second lowest by a rookie left tackle since 2018 (minimum 150 pass blocks), according to Next Gen Stats. "His job is to make sure that he's physically getting himself ready for what's next," offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said Thursday of Simmons "He's just got to focus one day at a time."

stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Alijah Vera-Tucker #75 of the New England Patriots looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots will be without Alijah Vera-Tucker for a minimum of four games. The organization officially placed the starting left guard on injured reserve in the hours leading up to Thursday night’s matchup against the Chicago Bears. Vera-Tucker, 27, had played 100 percent of the offensive snaps until sustaining a hamstring injury prior to halftime last weekend against his previous AFC East team. The former New York Jet went on to be listed as a non-participant on three consecutive injury reports before being ruled out for the Midwest road trip. Arriving on a three-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in March, Vera-Tucker stands six starts into his stay in Foxborough. The 6-foot-4, 308-pound USC product entered the NFL in the first round of the 2021 NFL draft at No. 14 overall. He has started all 49 of his career appearances, spending time on injured reserve in 2022, 2023 and 2025. Now the 13th current Patriot on IR, a return to the 53-man roster will have to wait until at least the bye week in late November. For the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at Soldier Field, New England elevated guard Xavier Newman-Johnson and outside linebacker Benton Whitley from the practice squad while leaving an open spot on the active roster. Newman-Johnson, 27, signed to the practice squad in September after being hosted at Gillette Stadium on a visit. The 6-foot-2, 297-pound interior offensive lineman stands 25 games into his NFL journey and has made a handful of starts. Originally entering the league with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022, Newman-Johnson spent parts of two campaigns with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former club. The Baylor product went on to make stops between the practice squad, 53-man roster and injured reserve of the Jets before heading elsewhere in the division. His career includes 338 snaps on offense and 68 snaps on special teams. Whitley, 27, joined New England’s 17-man scout team in September. The 6-foot-3, 255-pound edge rusher originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Los Angeles Rams in 2022. stories.summary: Former NY Giant Evan Neal lands with a division rival
stories.detailText: Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles have signed former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal to their practice squad. Neal had recently been released from the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, where he landed after being released in the Giants’ final cutdowns following the 2026 training camp. Neal, the 7th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, has been the biggest draft bust in recent memory for the Giants. He hasn’t played a regular season snap for the Giants since the 2024 season, when he filled in for Jermaine Eluemunor at right tackle. Eluemunor had originally been slated to play guard that year, but moved out to right tackle when Neal suffered an injury in camp. The Giants then converted Neal to guard in 2025, which was where he played in the 2026 off-season as well, but he never found his way to the field on game day. The Eagles’ decision to sign Neal comes as their offensive line is reshuffled by the retirement of RT Lane Johnson and the trade of OC Cam Jurgens. Philadelphia always seemed like a likely landing spot for Neal after he was released by the Giants. The Eagles have long prized size and power in their offensive linemen, both of which Neal has in spades. It remains to be seen if he’ll get the chance to compete for a starting job — or even be active on game days — as he attempts to salvage a once-promising career.

stories.title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Baltimore Ravens
stories.summary: Derrick Henry has to be a major point of emphasis this week for the Bengals.
stories.detailText: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore to face the Ravens at 1:00 pm ET this week. The Bengals are coming off a bye week, while the Ravens are coming off a close loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Ravens are currently a half game ahead of the Bengals in the division, sitting at 4-2 on the season. The Bengals are looking to drop the Ravens to 4-3 this year, while getting themselves to 4-2. Here are three keys to the Bengals winning in Baltimore for what would be their first AFC North victory of 2026. Slowing down Derrick Henry I have concerns about Justice Hill, carries to Zay Flowers on jet sweeps, and limiting either Lamar Jackson or Snoop Huntley when they break out of the pocket. The one guy that can really wear down a defense, though, is Derrick Henry. One of the best running backs of his era, Henry has 534 rushing yards already this season. He is coming off his lowest rushing total of the season, running for 58 yards against a strong Browns defense. Can the Bengals have similar success in slowing down Henry this week? To do so, they’ll have to get better at containing outside zone runs. Teams have been much more successful getting the ball to the perimeter instead of just running up the middle. Slowing down Henry will take a total team effort. The defensive line, linebackers, and secondary players will all need to bring their hard hats this week. Limiting Derrick Henry and the Ravens’ rushing attack will go a long way in pulling off the road victory. Create explosives in the passing game The Ravens are the 13th-best passing defense this season, allowing 210 passing yards per game. They are ranked 12th against the run. While they sit in the top half of the league against the pass, they haven’t faced a murderer’s row of passing attacks to start the year. The Ravens have played the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons, and Browns. The Cowboys are the only one of those teams ranked in the top 15 in passing yards per game. The Bengals have the 8th-best passing attack, averaging 260 yards per game so far this season. If I am Cincinnati, I am testing that secondary early and often on Sunday. Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase are the best wide receiver tandem in the league. Dohnte Meyers has been a revelation this season and is coming off his best couple of games. Colbie Young is expected back in the mix this week after returning from injury. While it would be nice to get the running game going, you should come out looking to create explosives in the passing game to open it up. Teams always run the ball more effectively with a lead. I would come out passing to get that early lead. Take your shots down the field, and let your playmakers go make plays. Limiting Trey Hendrickson Trey Hendrickson has been the Ravens best pass rusher. Even though he has missed a couple of games with a hand injury, he is still leading the team in pressures. Hendrickson has 20 pressures in just four games played, and has added two sacks so far this season. The Bengals are very familiar with what Trey Hendrickson can do as a pass rusher. I would expect to see a tight end lined up over beside Orlando Brown Jr. quite often throughout this game. You can expect to see chips from not only those tight ends, but also extra attention from the running backs when we are throwing the football. Limiting Hendrickson’s impact as a pass rusher will let the Bengals hit those explosives in the passing game. If they do those things, they can come out of Baltimore with a big divisional win this week. What is your biggest key to a Bengals win over the Ravens this week?

stories.title: NY Giants DC Dennard Wilson won’t tolerate ‘traitors to the defense’
stories.summary: Wilson critical of effort on some plays vs. Saints.
stories.detailText: Alvin Kamra of the Saints en route to a 31-yard touchdown reception vs. the Giants on Sunday. | Getty Images The New York Giants surrendered 34 straight points to the New Orleans Saints last Sunday. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was critical on Thursday of the effort of players he felt did not hustle to the ball, calling it “unacceptable” and calling them “traitors to the defense.” “A few plays got out, especially in the pass game, because of missed tackles. Then last week, we’re not happy, and I wasn’t happy with our effort running to the ball,” Wilson said. “We put some stuff on tape that was not characteristic of a New York Giant defense, and it’s unacceptable, and it will be changed. “I look at guys that don’t run [to] the ball, and I call them traitors because they’re traitors to the defense. At the end of the day, when you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field, you have to get somebody else on the field, or they have to correct their behaviors. Last week was one of those things where we did not, on every play, run to the ball, and it was unacceptable.” Wilson did not specify the play or plays he was referring to. He was adamant, though, that he won’t tolerate it. “The guys know it, and this week when you see them out there, they will be flying around 100 miles per hour with a hair on fire,” Wilson said. “It’s 11-1 when you play defense. It’s 11 guys humming to the ball, and when you don’t do that, you don’t erase plays. We had a few plays that got out on us. “Everybody’s hunting. It’s probably not a touchdown. You get them down on the ground. It’s not an explosive play. You eliminate explosive plays with energy and effort. That’s how you eliminate it.” This might be the play that annoyed Wilson the most: Had to be uncomfortable re-watching the Kamara touchdown in the film room… pic.twitter.com/FORqfv4rMa — Dan Duggan (@DDuggan21) October 22, 2026 Nickel cornerback Dru Phillips on Thursday took accountability for his part in the play. He said it was “embarrassing” to be called out in front of his teammates. “You have 10 other guys depending on you as well. You can’t expect just one guy to make a tackle,” Phillips said. “These guys are depending on you, and when you’re just not giving that hustle that you should be you feel like I let this person down, or I let everybody down. “There’s no excuse for it. I’ve gotta hustle.” The Giants were one of the worst tackling teams in the NFL in Week 6. Missed Tackles in Week 6 Data: @pfref pic.twitter.com/GGPjUBLUuK — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 22, 2026 “Last week was one of our worst tackling games for whatever reason,” Wilson said. Wilson said he has no issue calling out players “We confront everything,” Wilson said. “If you’re not doing something to help the team and you’re hurting the team, if your effort is bad, if you have a lack of toughness, it gets pointed out, and it gets pointed out in front of everybody. Not only in a defensive meeting, it gets pointed out in the full team meeting. “When you have behaviors that’s unacceptable, we’re not going to accept it. If you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.”

Las Vegas Raiders need Eric Stokes’ best performance vs. Puka Nacua in Week 7 key matchups against Los Angeles Rams
teamStories.summary: Two battles in the passing game and one in the rushing attack that will make a big difference on Sunday.
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 NFL season with very different expectations but find themselves entering the Week 7 contest in very similar situations. To a certain degree, this feels like a swing game for both clubs as the 3-3 Raiders and 2-4 Rams are clinging to playoff hopes as we approach the halfway point of the campaign. That adds importance to the key matchups below. Stokes vs. Nacua Even when Davante Adams was available, the Rams’ passing offense primarily ran through Puka Nacua. Despite missing two games, Nacua leads the team in targets (52) and receptions (37) while ranking second behind Adams in yards (417) and touchdowns (one), per Pro Football Focus . Now that Adams is on injured reserve , Nacua’s workload should increase even more. While the fourth-year pro doesn’t have blazing speed, he’s a very good route runner and one of the most efficient wideouts in the league. According to PFF , he ranks fifth at the position with 2.78 yards per route run so far this season, which would be just the third-highest YPRR he’s had during his four regular seasons. Also, that’s almost a full yard lower than Nacua’s 2025 figure ( 3.71 ). In other words, the BYU product is a tough cover that commands attention from the opposing defense’s top cornerback. That’s where Eric Stokes steps in for Las Vegas. After having a breakout performance last year, Stokes had a slow start this fall. He was targeted 24 times and allowed 15 receptions (62.5 completion percentage) for 209 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Weeks 1-5, per PFF , after yielding just a 56.0 completion percentage, 261 yards and one score over 16 games in 2025. However, the six-year veteran is coming off his best outing of the current campaign, surrendering just two catches on four targets for 29 yards to post a season-high 71.3 coverage grade against the Buffalo Bills’ high-powered offense. Diving even deeper, one catch and 23 of those yards came on a screen to running back James Cook, meaning Stokes only gave up one grab and six yards to the Bills’ receivers . So, there is a question of which version of the defense’s top corner the Raiders are going to get on Sunday. The lockdown perimeter defender from a year ago and last week, or the corner who seemed to struggle fitting into new defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s system? Obviously, the Silver and Black hope it’s the former. Granted, Nacua lines up all over the Rams’ offense with 109 snaps as a right outside receiver, 66 snaps on the left and 56 in the slot, per PFF , while Stokes is almost exclusively left outside corner ( 343 snaps out of 387 total, 88.6%). However, given that the Raiders are currently playing musical chairs at the other cornerback spot and the Rams don’t have many other notable receivers with Adams out, it’d make sense for Leonard to tweak his approach and have his top corner shadow Sean McVay’s top receiver on Sunday. Bowers vs. McDuffie It’s no secret that Klint Kubiak’s offense runs through “tight end” Brock Bowers. Like Nacua, Bowers missed two games and still leads his team in targets ( 40 ), receptions (28, tied with Michael Mayer) and receiving yards (382). He’s also tied with wide receivers Tre Tucker and Cody White for the team lead in receiving touchdowns with three. An “offensive weapon” is a more accurate description for the 2024 first-round pick since he’s only spent 15.8 percent of his pass snaps as an in-line tight end this season, according to PFF . As a result, opponents typically treat him like a ‘WR1’ by putting their top coverage defender on him. The Denver Broncos figured that out a few years ago with cornerback Patrick Surtain II, and several teams have followed suit, including the Bills last week. Buffalo did a decent job of keeping Bowers bottled up by matching him up against cornerback Christian Benford, resulting in just two catches for 23 yards on five targets . But when other defenders were covering Kubiak’s “football robot from heaven” a week ago, he hauled in two of three targets for 47 yards. So, expect the Rams to follow suit and go with a best-on-best matchup in the secondary. While the “Super Team” Los Angeles assembled this offseason hasn’t panned out so far, cornerback Trent McDuffie — who was acquired via a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs — isn’t part of the problem. The two-time All-Pro has been targeted 18 times but has yielded just five completions for a 27.8 completion percentage that ranks first among corners with at least 52 coverage snaps, according to PFF . That’s due in part to recording five forced incompletions at the third-highest rate (28 percent) for the position, resulting in the second-best coverage snaps per reception allowed (31.8) and second-highest coverage grade (88.7). Despite being division foes in 2024 and 2025, these two have only faced each other twice, with both matchups coming in Bowers’ rookie season since he was injured for both bouts against the Chiefs last year. The good news for the Raiders is that he had two catches for 48 yards on two targets against McDuffie that year, per PFF . So, the defensive back has been waiting about two years to get some payback. That being said, McDuffie missed last week’s game with a groin injury and sat out of Wednesday’s practice. So, there’s a chance McDuffie doesn’t play on Sunday. Dean vs. Rams’ RBs Circling back to Los Angeles’ offense, McVay will likely lean more heavily on the rushing attack without Adams, especially since he has a strong running back duo. Kyren Williams is still the Rams’ lead back with 80 carries for 393 yards and four touchdowns on the season. Additionally, he’s been one of the most efficient backs in the league, ranking tied for eighth (minimum 27 carries) with 4.9 ypc and 10th in EPA per rush (0.03), according to Sumer Sports . Meanwhile, Blake Corum has about half as many rushes (47) but has been just as efficient with 223 yards, 4.7 ypc (tied for 12th) and 0.07 EPA per attempt (fourth). In other words, L.A. has a potent rushing attack no matter who is in the backfield. That raises the importance of Nakobe Dean’s role on Las Vegas’ defense this week. Among linebackers with at least 44 snaps against the run, Dean ranks 23rd with a 70.3 PFF run defense grade this season. That’s due in part to ranking tied for 14th with 12 ‘ defensive stops ’ in that phase of the game. Additionally, the free agent addition is tied for the league lead in forced fumbles with three through six weeks. Corum hasn’t had much of a fumbling issue in the NFL, with just one (Week 2 of 2026) in his three-year career. However, Williams has coughed up the rock 11 times during the regular season in his five-year career, and had another fumble in the postseason a couple of years ago. To the latter’s credit, he’s only had one this fall (also in Week 2), but Dean will certainly be looking to test Williams’ ball security. In the passing game, Corum has never been much of a threat in the past. But he does have nine catches for 91 yards in 2026, and both of those figures are already career highs. That being said, Williams is still the bigger threat out of the backfield. He’s logged 141 career catches for 962 yards and nine receiving touchdowns , and ranks first (30), fourth (217) and tied for seventh (one) for those metrics among running backs this season. That’s where the Rams could have an advantage since Dean has had trouble covering running backs, drawing seven targets and allowing seven catches for 67 yards to the position this year, per PFF . That being said, he is an effective blitzer with six pressures on 19 pass rushes in 2026. Meanwhile, Williams has yielded five pressures on 54 opportunities — something Leonard might game plan for — but Corum has yielded just one on 21 opportunities. Long story short, we’re in for a good running back(s) versus linebacker matchup on Sunday in several phases of the game.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has had his ups and downs during his career. He started out as the franchise’s future tight end. That changed when the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers in 2024 and demoted him to a backup role. He struggled with personal issues and injuries over the next two seasons. Despite these events, the Raiders’ front office gave him a new deal. The deal shocked many in the NFL landscape, with an APY of $15 million over the next three years. People questioned why the team would give so much money to a backup tight end. After the first six games, the way the Raiders deploy their offense with Bowers and Mayer has it making complete sense. Mayer is the inline tight end for most snaps, and the team uses 12 personnel on most downs. Mayer has started the season with 266 receiving yards with 28 receptions and a touchdown. He is on pace for 753 yards, which is a high total for tight ends in the NFL. Against the Buffalo Bills, he had a career-high 95 yards on seven receptions, giving Kirk Cousins another option as the Bills tried to take away Bowers. It wasn’t just checkdowns, either; he made big plays downfield. On Sunday, he showed he could be a serious threat in the offense with a 28-yard seam-route catch. Michael Mayer would be a TE1 on a lot of teams. Adjust his route slightly to find the hole in the zone and Cousins hits him for a big gain. pic.twitter.com/Nc6XXNGnu4 — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) October 19, 2026 Mayer is happy with his role and is proving he is worth every penny. The Raiders have two tight ends who will be the catalyst for how Kubiak wants to execute his passing game.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 1, the Las Vegas Raiders revealed their new plan to manage Maxx Crosby’s play time. It has, for the most part, continued through the first six weeks of the season appears to be the way the team will manage their 29-year-old star pass-rusher moving forward. In Week 1, against the Miami Dolphins, Crosby played 82.1 percent of the season. He has since played between 80 percent and 91.7 percent of the defensive snaps. His per game average is 86 percent of the snaps. He played 89 percent in Week 6, his second highest total. So, Crosby is still, of course, playing the vast majority of the snaps, but it is noticably less than in the past. In the previous two seasons, Crosby played 100 percent of the snaps in 17 of the 27 games he played. He played 100 percent of the snaps in 10 of 17 games in 2023. But playing every snap of most games took its toll. Crosby missed the first seven games of his career in past two seasons and had off-season surgeries. Of course, a failed physical nixed his trade to the Baltimore Ravens in March. So, the Raiders became dedicated to giving Crosby some more in-game rest starting in 2026 and they appear to be sticking with that plan. Raider Nation, take the conversation everywhere! teamStories.detailText: NFL trade season is about to heat up -- the deadline is less than three weeks away (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET). We've already seen receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . dealt to the Texans , quarterback J.J. McCarthy moved to the Giants , cornerback Joey Porter Jr . sent to the Cowboys and center Cam Jurgens traded to Baltimore . And in the weeks to come, more trades will follow. Let's project some of them with 11 proposals that make sense for both teams involved. While deadline deals across all sports don't always have a dramatic impact on the games that play out afterward, 2025 was a clear case when moves in the NFL mattered. The Seahawks might not beat the Rams in the regular season without the addition of Rashid Shaheed , who kicked off their comeback victory with a punt return touchdown. That win pushed the Seahawks into position to land the top seed in the NFC, which gave them home-field advantage in the rubber match against the Rams -- and that might have made the difference in the NFC title game . Not a bad return for a pair of Day 3 picks. Teams with Super Bowl aspirations will be hoping to follow in Seattle's footsteps as the 2026 deadline approaches. If anything, I was a little concerned that there might not be many teams ready to trade away talent, given that 27 of the league's 32 teams still have at least a 9% chance of making it to the postseason after six weeks of football, per ESPN's Football Power Index . Then two things happened this week to shake up the trade market. One was the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard , which came after the Colts blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the Titans at home Sunday and lost 26-20 . Ballard endured some unfortunate luck given that his franchise quarterback (Andrew Luck) and one of his best draft picks ( Shaquille Leonard ) retired prematurely because of serious injuries, but the two big swings Ballard took toward the end of his tenure didn't work out, with QB Anthony Richardson Sr . and cornerback Sauce Gardner both failing to live up to expectations (so far) during their time with the Colts. Firing Ballard doesn't mean the Colts are about to trade off every veteran on their roster, especially given that the rest of the front office staff and head coach Shane Steichen still remain, but there's less of a mandate to try to win this season than there would have been with Ballard at the helm. Indy has several pending free agents who could be appealing to opposing teams, and there might be a scenario in which the 2027 version of this franchise has Mannings in the front office and on the football field. Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' And then in Philadelphia, we found out that quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season because of deep vein thrombosis. This was already beginning to feel like a lost season for the Eagles, who were missing as many as nine potential starters in Sunday's loss to the Panthers , but the news that Hurts won't be returning anytime soon only reaffirms that Philadelphia needs to start thinking about 2027. Barring a stunning turn from Tanner McKee , who struggled badly against Carolina, the Eagles don't have any sort of meaningful ceiling this season beyond potentially competing to win a moribund NFC East with a seven- or eight-win season. This is typically the time of year when GM Howie Roseman calls around on veterans to add to his roster in advance of a playoff push. This season, he's more likely to be the one fielding those calls, and he can't afford to be timid or unrealistic. This Eagles team was flawed even before the Hurts injury. The offensive line, which has long been at the core of so many great Philly teams, has fallen apart. With Lane Johnson retired , Jurgens traded, and questions about the future for Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen , the Eagles could need at least two and as many as four new starting linemen next offseason. They'll also need to work on contracts for young defensive standouts such as Quinyon Mitchell , Jalyx Hunt and Cooper DeJean , which will cause the Eagles to skew far more heavily toward spending on defense after going in the opposite direction. And factoring in the players we already expect not to be back on the roster in 2027, Philly could be at $80 million in dead money on next season's cap. Roseman could push money into the future to avoid problems there, but it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles try to create an advantageous situation in 2028 and beyond by taking a year to reset their cap, as they did in 2021. With a need to address multiple spots along the O-line, add depth on defense and potentially line up a long-term replacement for Hurts, Roseman has his work cut out for him over the next 12 months. Adding draft capital would help that process. It wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles listen to offers for their pending free agents, and we'll have a trade or two in that direction later in the column. I just wouldn't expect them to move cornerstone players such as Mitchell, DeVonta Smith , Jordan Mailata or Jalen Carter . I have to start today, though, with a player whose status on the 2027 roster is still up for grabs. Adding him was a masterstroke that elevated the roster and sank the hearts of Philly's division rivals. He was the perfect addition to the team in 2024. But ... is Saquon Barkley going to be on the Eagles in 2027? And if not, would Roseman consider trading his star RB in lieu of losing him for nothing as a cap casualty next offseason? Barkley was a deserving Offensive Player of the Year candidate in 2024, but he wasn't anywhere near as effective as a runner behind a much worse offensive line in 2025, averaging 4.1 yards per carry (down from 5.8). He has been in and out of the lineup in 2026 because of injuries and turns 30 in February. He's not likely to carry Philadelphia very far over the rest of the 2026 season, given that the line is missing multiple starters and the Eagles won't have their starting quarterback the rest of the way. Barkley is owed $16 million next year, $2.5 million of which is fully guaranteed. That's not an exorbitant sum for a great running back, but I'm not sure the Eagles as constructed in 2027 are going to be in position to get the most out of his talents in the way they were in 2024. Roseman might prefer to use that $16 million to fix what has gone wrong at the line of scrimmage and trust his ability to find a useful back in free agency or in the middle rounds of the draft, as Philly did for many years before the Barkley addition. I wouldn't fault the Eagles for holding on to Barkley, but Roseman won't hesitate to be aggressive if the right deal is out there. And while there aren't a ton of teams in the running back market, there's one who would make sense as a potential Barkley trade partner -- which is where I'll begin our annual list of pre-deadline trade proposals. Jump to a deal: MIN-PHI | CAR-PHI | DET-LAC PIT-LV | SF-IND | LAR-IND LV-JAX | CHI-TB | NYG-LAC KC-PHI | NE-WSH Vikings land an impact RB Vikings get: RB Saquon Barkley Eagles get: 2027 third-round pick (with conditions) At 5-0, the Vikings might very well be the team that's actually in position to benefit from adding a star back in his prime. Minnesota has a 90.9% chance of making it to the postseason, per ESPN's FPI, but it'll need the run game and a healthy back once it gets there. Jordan Mason has already hit injured reserve this season and has battled injuries in each of the past three years. Aaron Jones Sr . is 32 years old, has already left at least one game because of a knee issue and is on pace for 330 carries. The Vikings are 22nd in explosive play rate on designed runs, which is a reality of life with Jones in the fold. Adding Barkley would allow the Vikings to use him as their primary back while making Jones a complementary player, which is probably the right role for the veteran at this point of his career. Jones can catch passes and block, which would make him an upgrade on DeeJay Dallas , who currently plays that role. Barkley also makes just $867,000 or so over the rest of the season, making him an easy addition for the Vikings financially. Minnesota would be on the hook for a minimum of $2.5 million next year, although trading a third-round pick for Barkley means the Vikings would probably expect to keep him around in 2027. The Vikings have nearly $38 million in projected cap space next year , a figure that will rise dramatically after a simple restructure of Justin Jefferson 's deal, which currently has a $49.4 million cap hold. That figure doesn't include a quarterback, but the Vikings aren't likely to be paying top-level money for their signal-caller next season, especially if they're investing so much in the infrastructure around their starter. Trading a third-round pick for nearly two years of Barkley at a total cost of about $17 million would be a pretty reasonable bet for the Vikings to make given how well their defense is playing. Jones and Mason could be a solid one-two punch, but are you willing to count on them to be present, healthy and productive by the time we get to January? Are the Vikings comfortable using Dallas or Demond Claiborne as their lead backs if not? Barkley isn't the only running back who makes sense for the Vikings, and he has his own injury history to worry about, but he would certainly be the highest-upside option. In this case, the actual pick the Eagles would land in return would be subject to Barkley's play in Minnesota. The Vikings already own Philly's third-round pick as a result of the Jonathan Greenard trade , and that third-round pick projects to land at the 70th overall slot. Minnesota's own third-round pick projects to fall all the way to No. 93, which is a more dramatic difference than it might seem. Ben Baldwin's draft chart projects the difference between the 70th and 93rd picks as being worth about $6.5 million in surplus value over four years. So, the terms of this trade: If Barkley runs for 500 or more yards over the remainder of the regular season and the Vikings advance to the playoffs, the Eagles would land the better of the third-round picks (and the lesser if not). If he runs for at least 150 yards in the playoffs and the Vikings advance to the Super Bowl, the pick gets bumped up to a second-rounder. Trading Barkley would be bittersweet, and Roseman got to see how damaging moving on from him can be to a general manager's reputation from the other side of the coin two years ago. It's also realistic to suggest that Barkley isn't going to be able to play like the guy we saw in 2024 anytime soon in Philadelphia given the lack of infrastructure supporting the run game. If Roseman thinks Barkley is likely to be a cap casualty this offseason, trading him now makes sense. And even if that isn't the case, dealing Barkley for a Day 2 pick and using the cash savings elsewhere next offseason might not necessarily be a bad idea. Panthers boost their secondary Panthers get: CB Riq Woolen , 2028 sixth-round pick Eagles get: TE Ja'Tavion Sanders , 2028 fifth-round pick Woolen is another veteran who won't be back in Philadelphia next season. Signed to a one-year, $12 million deal to handle outside cornerback duties across from Quinyon Mitchell, Woolen hasn't gotten off to a great start in his new digs, allowing a 109.3 passer rating in coverage . During his time in Seattle, he allowed a 70.6 passer rating in coverage, making the Pro Bowl as a rookie. While Woolen can be susceptible to double moves and is tied with L'Jarius Sneed for the most penalties committed by a defensive player since the start of 2022, cornerbacks with his coverage ability and size (6-foot-4) aren't easy to find, especially in the middle of an NFL season. He's going to be best in a zone scheme where he can use that frame to take away throwing lanes on quick routes and make it difficult for quarterbacks to fit passes over the top. The Panthers are in first place in the NFC South, and while cornerback wasn't a need for them heading into the season, it has become one. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve , leaving Carolina down to Will Lee III , Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade at cornerback. The timetable for Horn and Jackson to return isn't clear, so adding a veteran would make plenty of sense. Panthers defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero also runs a scheme similar to Vic Fangio's in Philadelphia, which would make for an easy transition from Woolen's perspective. It also wouldn't cost Carolina much. Woolen will make just $840,000 plus incentives over the remainder of the season. The Panthers would be giving up a swap of Day 3 picks and a player buried on their depth chart in Sanders, who has been a healthy scratch throughout the 2026 season. Sanders had 33 catches for 342 yards and a touchdown as a rookie in 2024, but he didn't build on that performance in 2025 and hasn't even seen the field in 2026. With Grant Calcaterra and Dallas Goedert hitting free agency after the season, Philly has a hole at tight end. Eli Stowers projects to be the lead option as the move tight end, but Sanders has the size to play as a more traditional option and the athleticism to create after the catch. He won't turn 24 until March, is owed just $1.9 million combined over the next two years and can play on special teams, which would make Sanders a reasonable second or (preferably) third tight end option for the Eagles as they rebuild that room. Lions attack their defensive flaws Lions get: Edge Khalil Mack , CB Donte Jackson Chargers get: 2027 fourth- and sixth-round picks One of the few teams that is very obviously out of the playoff picture, the 0-6 Chargers are staring down a lost season. They're not about to tear down the roster given that Justin Herbert is still only 28 years old, but GM Joe Hortiz also finds himself in a position to move on from veterans who aren't likely to be on the roster in 2028 and beyond. Jackson fits that bill. The well-traveled cornerback played at a Pro Bowl level last season after going to the Chargers from the Steelers, making him one of many defensive backs to produce career years after joining up with Jesse Minter (who might very well be interested in adding him to play on the outside in Baltimore). This year, though, Jackson has been limited to 113 snaps by hamstring issues. Mack, who was considering retirement before returning to Los Angeles on a one-year deal, would also be an obvious trade candidate. At 35 years old, he is still a valuable edge defender for the Chargers. He has three sacks and six quarterback knockdowns through six games, and Mack's 5.0% quick pressure rate is still well above the league average of 3.9%. Mack has always been solid against the run, and he can step into any defense and be a viable, above-average edge rusher for the remainder of the season if he can stay healthy. Both players are free agents after the season, and there's a decent amount of money involved here. Jackson is owed $4 million over the remainder of the season, while Mack is due $5.3 million. NFL teams don't necessarily need to cut payroll in a lost season, but the Chargers wouldn't mind adding draft capital for two players who might not be back next season, especially if they can save millions of dollars in the process. They could alternately want to eat some of that money to add more draft capital in a potential trade and think the picks are a better use of the cash than players who would be playing out the string for a hopeless team. Guess who could use an edge rusher and a cornerback? The Lions. DJ Wonnum has a team-high five sacks as he takes advantage of defenses double-teaming Aidan Hutchinson , but Detroit could certainly use another edge rusher to take some of the workload off its two starters and provide some help if Hutchinson or Wonnum goes down. And the Lions are incredibly desperate for cornerback help, given that they're relying on the likes of Ennis Rakestraw Jr ., Rock Ya-Sin and Roger McCreary for meaningful snaps this season. Jackson would be a cut above those players and a viable second option alongside D.J. Reed , who has also struggled so far this season. In this deal, the Chargers eat about half of the money owed to Jackson and Mack over the remainder of the season, making the midseason cash expenditure more palatable for the Lions. The Lions have the league's second-best offense in terms of points scored per drive, but the defense needs help. And here Detroit adds two experienced starters on that side of the ball, giving the team a better shot at competing in what's going to be a dogfight in the NFC North. Steelers bring in a veteran on the back end Steelers get: S Isaiah Pola-Mao , 2028 seventh-round pick Raiders get: 2028 sixth-round pick Here's another defensive back with a realistic shot of being moved before the deadline. Pola-Mao started at free safety for the Raiders in 2024 and 2025 under then-coordinator Patrick Graham. Las Vegas signed the homegrown starter to a two-year, $7.6 million extension before the 2025 season, but second-round pick Treydan Stukes won the starting job in camp this summer, and the Raiders don't play many three-safety looks. Pola-Mao has played just 112 snaps this season, almost all of which came while Stukes missed part of Week 2 and all of Week 3 because of a concussion. Pola-Mao isn't a great player, but he's a viable safety in a pinch. And the Steelers seem to be in a pinch for safety help around this time every year. This time around, the organization quickly lost faith in veteran Rayshawn Jenkins , who has been on the scene of the crime for multiple disasters this season. Against the Browns , he missed a tackle on a Jaleel McLaughlin touchdown run, then appeared to rotate to the wrong side of the field on a 60-yard completion to Denzel Boston . He was benched shortly thereafter, didn't play a defensive snap over the two ensuing weeks and was released Wednesday. Pittsburgh is using Jaquan Brisker and rookie seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings at safety, with Jalen Ramsey playing in a hybrid slot/safety role. Brisker's injury history and Spears-Jennings' inexperience would suggest that the Steelers would be wise to at least add a veteran safety as depth. Trading Pola-Mao would save the Raiders $2.4 million over the remainder of 2026, a worthwhile amount for a team that doesn't see the fifth-year undrafted free agent as part of its future plans. 49ers add a run stopper 49ers get: DT Grover Stewart , 2027 seventh-round pick Colts get: 2027 sixth-round pick San Francisco fans are understandably dreaming about a reunion with DeForest Buckner , who was once dealt in the opposite direction between these two teams for a first-round pick, but I'm not sure that's as great of a fit as it might seem. The 49ers already have Osa Odighizuwa playing in that penetrating defensive tackle role, and rookie Gracen Halton has flashed alongside him, with sacks in each of the past two games. Buckner is still a great player, and I wouldn't fault the 49ers for just lining up as many superstars up front as possible and daring opposing offensive lines to simply figure it out, but this team really needs more help at nose tackle. San Francisco is 27th in success rate against the run so far this season. A year ago, it was 31st. The 49ers have been able to insulate themselves against run game issues by playing from ahead for most of the season, but they'll need to be better against the run by the postseason. Adding Stewart to the defensive line rotation would go a long way in helping San Francisco plug up those run game woes. The 33-year-old is a useful player and in the final year of his deal, but his contract is also expensive; he's owed $8.2 million in cash over the remainder of the season. The 49ers don't have cap concerns after restructuring some of their more significant deals, but that's a big cash outlay. They could encourage the Colts to absorb more of the money by offering a better draft pick, but with the 49ers still undefeated and fielding one of the oldest cores in football, I'd push ownership to spend now to try to build a team that can win a title. Stewart isn't the most exciting addition, but he's the sort of player the Niners need. Rams fix their kicking game Rams get: K Spencer Shrader Colts get: 2027 fifth-round pick In a crowded NFC West race, the Rams might look to throw draft capital at their kicking woes. Sean McVay is already on his third kicker of the season after cutting Harrison Mevis and losing Blake Grupe to injured reserve. L.A. just signed veteran Brandon McManus as a stopgap, but McManus missed three kicks in Green Bay's wild-card round loss to Chicago last season. Does McVay really want to go down that route? One solution would be trying to find a long-term option. Shrader bounced around the league early in his career, but he has found a home in Indianapolis. Over his career, the 27-year-old has gone 36-of-37 on field goals and 35-for-36 on extra points, including 6-for-6 on field goals over 50-plus yards this season. Playing his home games in a dome obviously helps, but Shrader is one of the league's most accurate kickers, and he won't be an unrestricted free agent until 2028. He is a useful player for the Colts, but he's also not an essential piece for a team that's rebuilding. And having dealt two first-round picks to the Jets for Sauce Gardner, Indy could use all the draft capital it can get. Raiders get an offensive playmaker Raiders get: WR Brian Thomas Jr . Jaguars get: 2027 second-round pick After months of denying that they were interested in trading Thomas, the Jaguars might have finally come to a breaking point with their former top wide receiver. Thomas caught zero passes during Jacksonville's two-game road trip in London. In the win over the Eagles , he wasn't able to get his feet down in the corner of the end zone for what could have been a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence . Then against the Texans , Thomas dropped an admittedly low throw from Lawrence that might have set the Jaguars up for a long field goal attempt just before halftime. Thomas didn't play a single snap in the second half of the loss to the Texans, and afterward, Jacksonville coach Liam Coen didn't hide his frustration. "Guys have to make plays," Coen said about the 2024 first-round pick. Travis Hunter , who played his largest offensive role of the season, made some of those plays in Thomas' absence. With the Jags committed to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers as starters, rookie Josh Cameron earning a larger piece of the rotation, Hunter's role potentially expanding, and Jacksonville wanting to play 12 personnel to get Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher on the field, there's just not a big role for Thomas at the moment. The Marvin Harrison Jr. trade established an asking price for Thomas. Harrison was a better prospect entering the league in the same draft class, which would make him more appealing to teams that really value their scouting reports. Thomas, on the other hand, has actually had a high-end season as a pro, racking up 1,282 yards as a rookie while catching passes from Lawrence and Mac Jones . I'm not sure there were a lot of teams lining up to trade a second-round pick for Harrison, but the Cardinals were able to find one. I expect that the Jaguars could also find one here. And at the right price, there should be a lot of teams willing to take a shot on Thomas, who has legitimate high-end speed and the ability to separate from man coverage. The Rams, who have pillaged Jacksonville for young players in the past, could very well see Thomas as a value addition and both a short- and long-term replacement for Davante Adams , who is out for two months and a free agent after the year. The most obvious candidate for a Thomas trade, though, would be the Raiders. Vegas still needs to add receiver help beyond tight end Brock Bowers for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza . Tre Tucker has been effective as a deep threat, but he's probably stretched as a primary wide receiver and will be a free agent after the season. Offseason addition Jalen Nailor , signed to a three-year, $35 million deal , has six catches in five games. Bowers is brilliant, and Michael Mayer has been a valuable in-line tight end, but coach Klint Kubiak needs a receiver who can both stretch the defense and run a full route tree. The Raiders' playoff chances are sub-10%, per the FPI, and barring a significant winning streak, they're not really in a place to add a short-term option for 2026. Thomas would be more of a long-term addition. He's owed $3.5 million combined over the next two years and would have a fifth-year option available for $17.2 million in 2028 . At $7 million per year over the next three seasons, Thomas would be making No. 3 receiver money for Las Vegas with the upside to be a potential lead option. Is there a risk in trading a second-round pick for a wide receiver who is frustrating the team that drafted him? Of course. The Bears traded a second-round pick for Chase Claypool , who was falling down the depth chart in Pittsburgh, and got 18 catches over two years from him before moving on. The Steelers used the pick they landed for Claypool -- which ended up being the top selection of the second round -- to draft Joey Porter Jr. The Raiders aren't likely to completely collapse over the rest of the season, but there's a chance that they end up sending a pick toward the top of the second round to the Jaguars for Thomas. Of course, the chance to add a potential star wideout for the quarterback-in-waiting also seems like a worthwhile risk to take. Bears find some edge-rush support Bears get: Edge Anthony Nelson , 2027 seventh-round pick Buccaneers get: 2027 sixth-round pick Speaking of Chicago, let's get it some extra depth on the edge. The Bears actually have a 9.8% sack rate when they rush four or fewer this season, one of the best rates in the NFL, but they're operating somewhere below 100%. Dayo Odeyingbo is on injured reserve , and Montez Sweat is serving a two-game suspension for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing drugs. Both will be back sooner rather than later, but nobody has ever gotten to the postseason and complained about having too many pass rushers. Nelson represents reasonable depth behind Odeyingbo, Sweat and Austin Booker , who leads the Bears with four sacks. Nelson has been a rotational player for most of his time with Tampa Bay, but the signing of Al-Quadin Muhammad , the selection of Rueben Bain Jr . in the first round of this year's draft and the surprising emergence of second-year pro David Walker has kept Nelson off the field. The 29-year-old has played just 12 of 139 possible defensive snaps over the past two weeks for the 1-5 Bucs. In addition, Nelson will make about $2.7 million over the rest of the season, which isn't going to be very appealing to the Bucs if he's taking most of his snaps on special teams. A competitive Bears team could integrate Nelson into the roster as the fourth edge rusher on game days. Bears fans might want someone like Josh Sweat , and I can understand why, but Chicago's pass rush has quietly been more effective than many expected heading into the season, which leads me to a more modest addition up front. Giants address their thin interior Giants get: DT Dalvin Tomlinson , 2028 seventh-round pick Chargers get: 2028 sixth-round pick Another veteran reserve for the Chargers who could be on the move between now and the deadline, Tomlinson would be coming full circle after starting his career in New York. The well-traveled defensive tackle isn't the interior disrupter we saw earlier in his career, but Tomlinson is also only two years removed from an 18-knockdown season with the Browns in 2024. He's a pending free agent with Los Angeles and due $2.1 million over the rest of 2026. The Giants started the season thin on the interior after trading away Dexter Lawrence II and losing Roy Robertson-Harris to a torn Achilles . New York has gotten by through adding veterans such as Shelby Harris and DJ Reader , and Tomlinson would be another defensive tackle in that vein. The only Giants DT with a sack this season is CJ Okoye , so even a modest contribution from Tomlinson while playing about 35-40% of the defensive snaps would go a long way. Chiefs think about the long and short term Chiefs get: TE Dallas Goedert Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick There has been talk about the Chiefs adding Tyreek Hill or another wide receiver as a replacement for injured Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton , and it's entirely possible that they add a wideout at some point before the end of the season. With Kansas City playing bully ball and building its offense around Kenneth Walker III , though, I wonder whether going in the opposite direction might be a better idea. K.C. already uses 12 or 13 personnel on nearly 40% of Patrick Mahomes ' dropbacks. So, what about adding another receiving tight end to the mix? Here, Chiefs coach Andy Reid goes back to his old employers to add a versatile playmaker in Goedert, who scored a career-high 11 touchdowns a season ago as one of the few players who seemed to thrive under offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo. Goedert is most efficient as a receiver out of the slot, but he can also work inline as a blocker or pass catcher. He would give Kansas City some leverage against the possibility of Travis Kelce slowing down as the season goes along and work alongside the future Hall of Famer as a potential mismatch over the middle of the field. Goedert will make just $870,000 over the remainder of the season, so the Chiefs won't have any financial trouble fitting him onto their roster. The longtime Eagles standout is a free agent after the season, and he's likely to be replaced in the long term by rookie second-round pick Eli Stowers, who began the season on injured reserve. Chiefs GM Brett Veach might be reticent to trade draft picks for short-term options after moves for players such as DeAndre Hopkins haven't necessarily paid off in recent years, but Goedert could also be the replacement for Kelce as the primary tight end in Kansas City if he signs a new deal after the season. Patriots pad their OL depth Patriots get: OL Andrew Wylie , 2027 seventh-round pick Commanders get: 2027 sixth-round pick It's rare to see a team nearly run out of linemen in an NFL game, but the Patriots came close last week. With Mike Onwenu already sidelined and Will Campbell playing despite a knee injury , New England lost Alijah Vera-Tucker , Morgan Moses and Ben Brown during a win over the Jets , leaving the defending AFC champs with a mere five healthy offensive linemen. The line made it through the rest of the contest, and Moses could be back this week, but the Patriots are remarkably thin up front. Adding a versatile lineman to the mix makes a lot of sense. Wylie can play right tackle or either guard spot, allowing him to fill in across the lineup with relative ease. He's buried on the Commanders' depth chart and has played just 15 snaps this season despite the absence of left tackle Laremy Tunsil , which caused Brandon Coleman to move to the left side. With multiple sixth-round picks, the Patriots can afford to ship one off to add a veteran. And the Commanders could turn to practice-squaders Trent Scott or Esa Pole , who filled in for the Chiefs at left tackle last season, as their swing tackle after Wylie's departure.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The ebbs and flows of an NFL season have always been funny to me. Three weeks ago, it felt like everyone was happy with the Las Vegas Raiders . Then, a three-game losing streak happens, and the mood shifts to doomsday prepping! I get it, though. A lot of people (myself included) got their hopes up with an undefeated start in September, only to get let down with a disappointing October so far. But the Raiders have a good opportunity to get back on track against a very hobbled Los Angeles Rams team in Week 7. All of that should give us plenty to talk about for this week’s mailbag. As always, anything Raiders-related is on the table and fire away with anything that’s on your mind. Send your questions my way by either dropping a comment in the comments section below, tweeting at me ( @MHolder95 ) or via email at SBPQuestions1@gmail.com . I’ll follow up with another column in the coming days. If you don’t have a commenting account already, you’ll need to create one but the steps are pretty easy and it’s a seamless process. Also, we have full-time moderators to enforce the Community Guidelines.
